items.body: You won’t come back for me calling was an SOS one more stop for me one more stop for more There are songs about heartbreak that behave as though somebody ought to erect a marble statue afterward, and then there are songs like SOS, where Barcelona trio Low Blows seem more interested in the miserable logistics of having cared too much. You call. Nobody comes. You try again. Eventually affection begins to resemble a bad financial decision, and the sensible course of action appears to be locking your heart somewhere nobody can get at it, including yourself. That is a rotten way to live, of course, which is precisely why the song feels convincing. Carlos Vergara’s bass carries a lot of the burden here, moving with the blunt authority of somebody dragging furniture across an apartment at three in the morning. Rubén Carballo’s drumming keeps the floor firm beneath it, while Andrés Silgado’s guitar scratches at the perimeter, sometimes bright, sometimes abrasive, never hanging around merely to decorate the walls. The electronics slip through the gaps, giving SOS a slightly unreal temperature. The band’s industrial, darkwave, new wave, and shoegaze tendencies remain visible, though Low Blows sound increasingly comfortable letting those elements collide without stopping to announce which shelf each one came from. Vergara’s vocal delivery makes the emotional shutdown feel almost practical. Love has become excessive, softness carries consequences, and whatever emergency prompted the original cry for help has already curdled into weary acceptance. The final image of a heart shut inside a box sounds less like melodrama than somebody explaining the storage arrangements after the relationship has been cleared out. Carlos Vergara’s video gets considerably stranger. He takes public-domain footage from Stella Simon and Miklos Bandy’s 1927–28 film Hände: Das Leben und die Liebe eines Zärtlichen Geschlechts and drops its expressionist hands into Low Blows’ world. Fingers grasp, palms open, bodies overlap, and images of the trio pass beneath these enormous gestures from another era. Suddenly a nearly century-old experimental film has become an accomplice to a post-punk song made by three musicians scattered between Ibiza, Mataró, and Vitoria-Gasteiz. That accidental collaboration across ninety-nine years is wonderfully appropriate, as SOS revolves around reaching toward someone and discovering that the distance remains. Watch the video for SOS below: Since Cruel appeared in 2020, Low Blows have tightened their approach considerably. Go! brought producer Matteo Vallicelli of The Soft Moon into their orbit in 2024, followed by an OMBRA Festival appearance. Vallicelli returned for the trio’s new self-titled album, mastered by Maurizio Baggio at La Distilleria. Low Blows have found an ugly, elegant little groove in which emotional damage can dance without pretending it has recovered. Listen to SOS below and order the single here. Low Blows by Low Blows Follow Low Blows: Instagram Facebook Bandcamp Soundcloud YouTube The post “I Locked My Heart Inside a Box” — Barcelona Post-Punk Trio Low Blows Share Video for “SOS” appeared first on Post-Punk.com.
items._genre: post-punk / darkwave / industrial / shoegaze / new wave
items._cn_summary: 巴塞罗那三人组Low Blows以新单曲《SOS》延续其冷峻的情感叙事。歌曲聚焦于一段感情的消亡过程——从无人回应的呼救，到最终将心锁进盒子的疲惫接受。Vergara的低音承担了主要骨架，以拖拽重物般的钝重权威推动情绪；Carballo的鼓点维持稳定的地基；Silgado的吉他游离于边缘，时而明亮时而刺耳，拒绝充当装饰。电子音色从缝隙中渗入，为整体增添些许超现实温度。乐队将工业、暗潮、新浪与自赏的元素不加解释地碰撞在一起，听感上更趋成熟。MV取材于1927-28年Simon与Bandy的表现主义默片《Hände》，近百年影像与当下后朋克形成跨越时空的对话。新同名专辑由The Soft Moon的Matteo Vallicelli制作，La Distilleria的Maurizio Baggio负责母带，呈现一种允许情感创伤坦然起舞的粗糙优雅。

items.body: A confession to begin: I�ve been a fan of Alison Cotton�s music for quite a while, so the announcement of a new album definitely brought me a frisson of delight. The Gods Laugh certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody over the constant underpinning of a lulling drone. While the playing revolves around her usual arsenal of viola, harmonium, hammered dulcimer, and piano, along with some percussion, on this album she also adds some drums, bass and synthesizer. The music is often improvised and captured in a single take, with an almost mystical, hushed sensibility that seems to reach through time, as with �I Still Know You are Calling My Name,� where the tune could have been plucked from an old folk song. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The centerpiece, however, is �Sprigs of Heather,� with an opening that recalls medieval sacred music that becomes a simple, slowly cascading, piano-led melody. It�s far from the longest track on the album, but a little pearl of perfection that carries the listener away. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh is a memorial of sorts to Cotton�s father, who died in late 2024. There�s a sense of loss reaching across these tracks, most specifically present on �The Final Harvest,� a solemn piece about her father�s last visit to the allotment he loved so much. It�s suffused with tenderness that extends beyond words. Light and darkness bleed into each other across the music, and moods shift. It�s music that happily stands beyond category, with hints of so many things, but ultimately standing as Alison Cotton music, which might well be all the definition it needs. It will challenge you but also satisfy and move you. What more can you wish from music? Find the artist online. More to hear: United States of Alchemy - Songs of Compassion (Review) Dani Jan� - Vida (Review)

items.body: Those of us who have been digging into Analog Africa�s increasingly formidable releases over the last two decades are well aware of the massive amount of raw, vodun-based Sato and Sakpata-derived funk the label has issued by Benin�s most prolific 1970s-era band, the Orchestre Poly-Ritmo. AA has dropped no fewer than 3 compilations of their heaviest material, as well as a reissue of the band�s first LP, in an effort to give them the international status they deserve. That being said, what might be different about this collection of their music? And who is Antoine Dougb�? Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa As it turns out, Dougb� was a song-conjurer whose mode of musical transfer was slapping his legs in a rhythm known as Cavacha, a groove created by drummer Belobi Meridjo, who was inspired by a train cadence that he worked into a pattern that ultimately spread like a 21st century California wildfire throughout Congolese pop music in the mid-1970s. Dougb�, known as the �Devil�s Prime Minister,� was also a practitioner of vodun who inspired fear in any musician he felt was unsuited to play his music, which is how he landed on working exclusively Poly-Ritmo, as he felt they could nail what he wanted in ways other bands couldn�t. His recording career was brief - 3 albums and a few singles - but as this collection shows, it was potent. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa Because of the era from which this music dates, it�s not surprising that the recording and instrument tones have changed - the guitars have a plastic sheen and synthesizers appear- even if the music remains rooted in the 1970s. Perhaps the influence of the Cuban son is more apparent here than on other Poly-Ritmo collections, especially in the collection�s initial offerings. And yes, Congolese rumba, then shaking all of sub-Saharan Africa to its knees, is present too. �Ma Won Min Towe Leo� is one example. Opening with a bed of synthesizers, the shimmering guitars, tinny, seemingly squeezed dry by the 80s themselves, lock in over relentless high-hat-focused grooves. The guitars finally start firing in different directions midway through, before that synth weaves back in, forming a bed underneath it all. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa �We Tayi Sin Assi Tche� is much more overtly Cuban. With its insistent cowbell, classic, nasal vocal call and response, and tight, repeated guitar figures, its debt to mid-twentieth century Afro-Cuban sons is transparent. Another track, �Djomido Ma Dougbe Tche� rides a groove reminiscent of 70�s-era Franco classic �Liberte.� The pulse is relentless, and the guitar solo repeats a tight repetition of a few notes, driving listeners to ecstasy all the while. However, none of this music is a mere copy of its influences; rather, like so much potent pop coming from the continent at the time, it is a swirl of major influences rendered by local rhythms and vocal phrasing to give it specific identity, in this case, to Benin. Dougb�s musical role on this collection is a bit murky. One of his three albums has a photo of him, fully mic�d behind a collection of hand drums, so perhaps he served as a percussionist/vocalist; this release never explains. He wasn�t a songwriter in the traditional sense. It seems he was more of an instigator and arranger, but his thumbprint was apparently heavy enough to warrant his name on the records he was involved with. Whatever the case, in his brief run as a recording artist, he and Poly-Ritmo produced a handful of driving, Cavacha-inspired grooves that can still wear holes in club floors. Further reading: Petrona Mart�nez - Ancestras (Review) Gnonnas Pedro & His Dadjes - Roi De L'Agbadja Moderne 1974-1983 (Review)
items.label: Analog Africa
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑聚焦贝宁传奇乐队Orchestre Poly-Rythmo与歌手Antoine Dougbé在1977至1982年间的合作录音。Dougbé以腿部拍击的Cavacha节奏著称，这一节奏源于鼓手Belobi Meridjo对火车节律的提炼，后广泛传播于刚果流行乐中。作为伏都教信仰者，Dougbé只与Poly-Rythmo合作，认为只有他们能准确诠释其音乐理念。专辑中吉他带有塑料质感的光泽，合成器开始出现，古巴松的影子在开篇曲目中尤为明显，刚果伦巴的元素也贯穿其中。以《Ma Won Min Towe Leo》为例，合成器铺垫之上，闪亮吉他与密集踩镲节奏交织，中段吉他向不同方向延展。以《We Tayi Sin Assi Tche》为代表的作品则更直白地呈现古巴风骨，铿锵牛铃与鼻音对唱形成经典对话。

items.body: After the extra-terrestial explorations of Eventyrferd , the previous album from Norway's Camilla Hole Trio, in which sci-fi synth sounds were married with traditional material, their latest release Langs is rather more earthbound. But the quest to look beyond their own country's folk music continues. Camilla Hole's main instrument being the soprano sax, the influence of jazz is unsurprising and this is evident in the opening track �Springleik,� signifying a tune used to accompany the springleik dance from the west of Norway. Initially Hole takes the melody with Egil Kalman and Knut Kvifte Nesheim providing rhythmic support on double bass and drums respectively, with the overdubbing of Kalman's modular synth and Nesheim's vibraphone adding colour. But characteristically for this trio, in which assigned roles are never clearly defined or adhered to, things soon start to move around, with Kalman taking up the melody on his bass, playing the melody in unison with Hole, while Nesheim opens things out further rhythmically. As the whole piece takes on a much more improvisatory feel, Hole plays the melody one more time as things draw to a close. Langs by Camilla Hole Trio

items.body: Sendas by Omar Sosa True to a Monk-inspired commitment never to play the same thing twice, Cuban pianist and composer Omar Sosa�s Sendas (Pathways), his latest solo offering, is the vivid invention of a pensive, restlessly creative, evolutionary artistry. As with all Sosa�s work, Sendas is the fortunate product of serendipity. In 2021 the COVID lockdown was underway, his marriage was ending, and a scheduled Milan appearance cancellation garnered an invitation to record at the Fazioli Pianoforti Concert Hall, annex to the renowned Italian piano manufactory in Sacile, Pordenone, about an hour northeast of Venice. At Fazioli, Sosa found himself in august company. Herbie Hancock and a host of classical pianists are Fazioli artists. Among the institutions that have embraced the Fazioli sound are the Juilliard School, Teatro La Fenice (Venice), the Budapest Palace of Arts, the Paris Conservatory, the Beijing Grand Theatre, and the universities of Salzburg, Graz, and Vienna. An unscripted two-hour solo improvisation on a Fazioli grand in the empty concert hall provided the raw audio for Sendas , later to be flavored in the mix, sparsely, with voice clips, percussion, loops, field recordings, found sounds effects that Sosa has collected over a career spanning four decades. As Sosa related to me soon after completing the post-production of Sendas , �Humanity is spiritually lost. We humans are all in this together. We need to evolve, but always keeping the traditions, walking with a strong, determined pace. We need more grounded music with overtones that resonate with the lower chakras� like throat singing, a mantra of the universal music.� �Creativity is about combining all your influences in a new way. I don�t aspire to be jazz, Latin, timba, reggaeton, classical. I avoid styles, but I respect the forms.� �I try not to think about how listeners will receive it but I do try to address their expectations, and go with the music to some other new place. Many free spirits come to listen, to be a part of the journey we are on.� Sosa laughs, �My son says, �Your niche is really small.� But the people who come really are there to be part of what we are going to do.� �Economics, technology, the streaming ear wash, algorithms all want to put you into a defined category � and so do many music journalists! The industry�s mentality is that any investment in artists must be defined by market categories to be profitable.� �But I play to be free of that,� Sosa says. �I play without thinking. There are no wrong notes. I love the first take. That�s the take, the natural voice of your soul. �Less is more� is a mantra in my life and music.� Consider the opening of �Inside the Spirit,� easing in leisurely, reaching over the keyboard into the resonant heart of the instrument, plucking and stroking the strings, teasing out a fuller resonance � only later to be embellished in the studio mix with light percussion and the muted Spanish-language refrain of a pregonero or street vendor, as might be heard in the calles of Havana or any other Latin American barrio. Sendas by Omar Sosa Moving from the secular to the sacred, �Deities Serenade� is an Afro-Cuban invocation of the shape-shifting divine, yet with ample room for ecumenical recasting in accord with a listener�s own self-location. �Inside My Soul� and �Something from Home� are Sosa works that to my ear may be an intuitive response to the distant call of Chopin�s "Nocturnes," to which Sosa says he listened every night for two years as a conservatory student in Cuba. Sendas by Omar Sosa �Caribbean Movement� and �Shirma� speak to Sosa�s rootedness in the lyrical, rhythmic, and harmonic heritage of the plantation islands where African and European cultures tragically entwined. In the violent forging of the world�s first truly modern people, social, cultural, linguistic, and musical displacements proved more flexible and accommodating than many of those same people, who shaped a contentious convergence of traditions into a changing same that persists into the unfolding present, ever yet to come. With expressive transcendence such as this, seeking to reduce the spiritual essence and inspiration of Sosa�s music to words is rather a fool�s errand. Better rather to listen, to contemplate, to perceive the pathway, to wander the sonic sendas coursing to the next way station without prejudice or preconception. To that end, Scott Price, Sosa�s longtime manager and friend relates, �We are using Sendas as the springboard for our first experiments in AI-generated Omar Sosa music videos.� Absent the opportunity to see and hear Sosa perform live, the palpable ideal, these ancillary audiovisual experiments further the ineffability of his artistic quest, the unique nature of the listening experience and all that ensues.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是古巴钢琴家 Omar Sosa 在意大利 Fazioli 钢琴厅进行的完整两小时独奏即兴录音，后来在后期制作中稀疏地加入了人声采样、打击乐、循环音、实地录音和拾得音效。Sosa 受 Thelonious Monk 影响，从不重复演奏同一段音乐，Sendas 体现了这种不断进化、拒绝被归类的创作哲学。他在采访中明确表示不追求爵士、拉丁、timba、reggaeton 或古典等任何风格标签，尊重形式但回避风格界定。专辑录音环境为意大利顶级手工钢琴厅，乐器本身的共鸣与演奏者的即兴融为一体。后期叠加的声响元素为钢琴独奏增添了层次感与仪式感，与 Sosa 所追求的'扎根音乐'及与低脉轮共振的理念相呼应。

items.body: Review by XixoTheRock — "Universo rojo"s social media accounts have been dead since 2021, the band, located in Vi�a delMar, apparently has no plans of coming back together in the near future, I must admit, that just asthere's a mystery around this LP (I will later tell you why!), it remains a mystery why they justdissapeared from social media for 5 years now!The band hands us this record in a silver platter, claiming that it is a conceptual record, indeed Icould see where they are going, the way the album sounds is overall telling of the nature of therecord itself, yet, and now I'll tell you the mystery, there's almost no lyrics! It's a semi fullyinstrumental album, with the only spoken sections being some indigenous like chants on the secondtrack "Visi�n planetaria de los tiempos", which seem to be in a native American language, I'd say itmost likely is Mapudungun, however, these chants and lyrics have no subtitles available on thedescription of the track (at least on platforms such as Spotify), and the singer seems to beuncredited, ladies and gentlemen this is the mystery I told you about! What do these lyrics meanexactly, and who sang them? It's captivating how a detail so simple can imply so many things!Musically wise, the music delivers an interesting experience which mixes krautrock with psychedelicrock and some elements of Zeuhl. Speaking of Zeuhl, it seems to be one of the main genres the bandlooks up to, as their publicly available playlist is dominated by bands such as Magma and Weidorje,as well as kasutrock acts like Popol Vuh and Amon D��l II, interestingly enough, we find some ratherodd influences that stand out in their playlist, like the extreme doom metal band Sunnata. Beinghighly influenced by classic experimental genres characterized by their use of symphonicinstrumentation, tape effects, spiritual topics and repetitiveness, "Impermanencia" is full ofsynthetizers, tape loops, repetitions of bass lines and riffs and a very hypotonic, spiral like windof textures and noises, all contributing to the creation of pieces which feel less like music andmore akin to a state of trance and meditation, albeit a very chaotic one. Each composition feelsvery much like the previous one, with little variation in the state it indices on the listener, thisoverall calmer and more meditative approach to music, will appeal to those invested in ambient andkraut, but won't satisfy those who prefer Zeuhl or more expressive, grandiose symphonic rock. The album has a lot of influences, although most can't be felt, but when it shows the signs, itsounds great! I'd like to point out that I was fairly dissapointed, as I was promised a magnum opus,a masterclass for the genre and most of the times, the record feels like an experiment halfway doneor a very relaxing jamming session.The musicianship is good enough, you can feel that each instrument was recorded separately and thenpieced together with the others, they are talented players but you can't really feel much chemistrybetween the parts that make the music, if you add this to what I previously stated, you get the fullpicture : this record is much more like something "Stars of the lid" would do if they went a littlemore experimental and not something that comes out of the chaotic mess of Zeuhl or the mathematicsof krautrock.My biggest issue with this record is the production, which is straight up unbearable...this recordsounds muddy, grainy, blurry and inconsistent, because yes, some tracks have good production and theother an awful one, and the difference is so noticeable it makes it uncomfortable to listen to. Thedrums can't even be heard most of the time, a record so inspired by krautrock should have a veryclear rhythmic direction and presence, which can't be heard through at least half of the record.I give it 2 stars because it's an interesting record to dig into and because of how hypnotic anduseful for meditation it is, but musically itself, I don't really see much to highlight...it'salmost as if it were an experiment that was never properly finished, this is sad because thisproject had so much potential.
items._genre: psychedelic rock / krautrock / space rock / zeuhl
items._cn_summary: 智利乐队Universo Rojo的第二张专辑《Impermanencia》是一张以器乐为主的迷幻太空摇滚作品，融合了Krautrock的循环律动、Zeuhl的混沌结构与南美原住民文化元素。专辑中第二轨使用了疑似Mapudungun语的原住民吟唱，但歌手身份和歌词内容均未公开，形成了一种神秘的仪式感。音乐以合成器音色、磁带循环、低音线条重复为核心，营造出冥想与恍惚交织的声场氛围，每首曲目状态趋同，更像是一场放松的jam session而非精心策划的杰作。乐手演奏技巧扎实，录音各乐器分别录制后拼合，虽显实验性但被评论者认为仅完成了一半的构想。整体适合偏好冥想型氛围和Krautrock的听众，但对追求Zeuhl力度或宏大交响摇滚的爱好者而言略显平淡。

items.body: California duo Antania release the single and video “33”, the first taste of their new album The Unholy 33, due 16 October 2026 via Argonauta Records. The digital album follows, with physical CD and vinyl editions to be detailed later. Antania, the project of Doc Luna and Kali Mortem, build “33” entirely without conventional guitars or bass, relying instead on synthesizers, distorted textures and machine-like rhythms. The duo describe their sound as avant-garde black metal filtered through industrial and experimental electronics, citing Dødheimsgard, Mysticum and Thorns alongside the dark electronic legacies of Skinny Puppy and Ministry as reference points. “The Unholy 33” runs eleven tracks: “33”, “DVHM3R”, “Sn0wAnGeL”, “Gloomzday”, “ThUgG33”, “Cykl0pZ”, “Flies”, “AntVniV”, “Frazzledrip”, “Kultz” and “HEarSe”. Following the album’s release, Doc Luna and Kali Mortem head to Asia in support, joining Swedish extreme metal act The Crown for dates in the UAE, Japan and South Korea, followed by an appearance alongside Evergrey in India. About Antania Antania is the Californian duo of Doc Luna and Kali Mortem. The project began as a doom-bass act, releasing the debut album “Lividity” in 2023 before signing with Triad Records later that year. Antania supported Psyclon Nine on a 2024 European tour alongside Devil M. “The Unholy 33” marks the duo’s move to Argonauta Records and a shift toward the avant-garde industrial black metal sound built entirely from electronics.

items._cn_summary: 加州双人组Antania发布新专辑《The Unholy 33》首支单曲及MV，整张专辑将于2026年10月由Argonauta Records发行。专辑最显著的特点是完全摒弃传统吉他和贝斯，仅依靠合成器、失真音色和机械化节奏构建声响，定位为先锋黑金属与工业电子的交叉地带。Doc Luna与Kali Mortem受Dødheimsgard、Mysticum、Thorns等北欧黑金属以及Skinny Puppy、Ministry等暗潮工业影响，试图用纯电子手段重塑极端金属的质感。全碟收录十一首曲目，命名采用数字与符号混合的拼写方式。发行后二人将随The Crown赴亚洲巡演。Argonauta Records是专注地下金属的小众厂牌，符合独立发行标准。

items.body: Naples dark folk act Corde Oblique released the single “Emma” on September 11, 2026, the first track from their tenth studio album, “All’ombra dei fanciulli in fiore” (In the Shadow of Young Girls in Flower), due November 27 on German label Dark Vinyl Records. The title references Marcel Proust and centers on parenthood. Emma by Corde Oblique ‘Emma’ previews a 12-track album recorded in Naples and mastered at Abbey Road Corde Oblique, led by composer and art historian Riccardo Prencipe, recorded “All’ombra dei fanciulli in fiore” between Peppino di Capri’s Splash Studios in Naples and London, where it was mastered at Abbey Road Studios by Alex Wharton. The album runs 12 tracks plus a bonus track, mixed by Massimo Aluzzi, and moves across metal, prog rock, folk songwriting and dark wave elements. The band’s core lineup on the record is Prencipe on classical and electric guitar, Alfredo Notarloberti on violin, Alessio Sica on drums, Umberto Lepore on bass and Rita Saviano on vocals. Guest contributors include singer-songwriter Andrea Chimenti, a voice of the Italian New Wave scene, on three tracks, and actress Maddalena Crippa, who provides a spoken-word performance. The digipak and booklet use vintage 1980s photographs of Pozzuoli and the Campi Flegrei (Phlegraean Fields), tying the album to the region where it was recorded. Corde Oblique open a promotional tour on October 24 at the Schwarzer Herbst Festival in Löbau, Germany, followed by Italian dates at Teatro Bolivar in Naples on November 20 and at Improve in Castelfranco Veneto on November 21. About Corde Oblique Corde Oblique is an Italian dark folk project founded and led by Naples-based composer and art historian Riccardo Prencipe. Side-Line has followed the band’s output since at least 2018, and covered their 2020 album “The Moon Is a Dry Bone.” “Emma” and the accompanying album “All’ombra dei fanciulli in fiore” mark the band’s tenth full-length and its first new release on Dark Vinyl Records, continuing a catalog built on the intersection of classical guitar, folk songwriting and darker, heavier textures.

items._cn_summary: 意大利那不勒斯暗潮民谣乐队Corde Oblique发布第十张录音室专辑《All'ombra dei fanciulli in fiore》（在少女倩影下），标题取材自普鲁斯特，主题围绕父母身份展开。专辑横跨金属、前卫摇滚、民谣创作与暗潮元素，器乐编制包含古典吉他、电吉他、小提琴、贝斯与鼓，并加入客座人声与口语表演。录音在Peppino di Capri的Splash Studios完成，后期在伦敦Abbey Road Studios母带处理。唱片包装采用1980年代拍摄的Pozzuoli与弗莱格瑞地区老照片，与那不勒斯地域文化形成呼应。乐队由作曲家兼艺术史学者Riccardo Prencipe领导，融合古典吉他与暗色调重型质感，呈现跨流派特征。

items.body: Projekt Records releases Norwegian ambient musician Erik Wøllo‘s new album Earthshine on 18 September 2026. The album is available as a Pay What You Can digital release and as a CD limited to 300 copies, packaged in a 4-panel digipak. Earthshine by Erik Wøllo The title refers to earthshine, the sunlight reflected from the earth’s surface that faintly illuminates the part of the moon not directly lit by the sun. Across 20 short tracks that crossfade into one another, “Earthshine” moves through abstract electronic soundscapes built from processed drones and sequencer pulses, alternating between expressive passages and sparser, hushed sections. The CD edition also includes a 21st, gapless version of the full album as a single continuous piece. Wøllo recorded the album to analog 4-track and 8-track tape machines before transferring the material to computer for further arranging and mixing, a return to the recording approach he used in the 1980s. Explaining why he went back to tape for “Earthshine”, Wøllo said: “When the tape is running, something affects me, I descend into myself, realizing music completely in the moment. I wanted to go back to the way of recording I was into in the 1980s, using old analog tape recorders. How would it affect my compositional process? Would it take me in other compositional directions? Compare it to writing a novel with a pencil instead of a computer. The unhurried measured approach was more time-consuming and led me to make different creative choices. It turned out that the music became more fluid and open-ended.” Beyond the Projekt Records Bandcamp page, “Earthshine” is also available through Projekt’s distribution partners deejaydead.de, littleuniversemusic.co.uk and audioglobe.it. About Erik Wøllo Erik Wøllo was born on 6 January 1961 in Hemsedal, Norway. He started playing guitar at age 11 and began his professional career in 1980, touring Norway in jazz, rock and fusion bands before turning to a full-time solo career in 1984, when he built his own studio, Wintergarden. His third album, “Traces” (1985, Cicada Records), marked a turning point toward the guitar-and-synthesizer-based ambient and space music style that has defined his solo work since. Wøllo has released more than 50 solo albums, moving through labels including Origo Sound, Monumental Records and Spotted Peccary Music before settling with Projekt Records, which has issued his work since “Gateway” (2010) and remains his current label. His catalog includes “Silent Currents” (2011), “Different Spaces” (2017), “Recurrence” (2021), “Sojourns” (2022) and “Snow Tides” (2026), among others. He has also released collaborative albums with Steve Roach (“Stream of Thought”, 2009, and “The Road Eternal”, 2011), Michael Stearns (“Convergence”, 2020), Ian Boddy (“Frontiers”, 2012, “Meridian”, 2018, and “Revolve”, 2023), and Byron Metcalf (“Earth Luminous”, 2016), among others. “Revolve”, made with Ian Boddy, won the Schallwelle Award for best ambient album in 2023. Wøllo contributed a rework to Apoptygma Berzerk’s 25th-anniversary album “SDGXXV”, having worked with the band in the studio during the making of their 1993 debut “Soli Deo Gloria”. He has also performed at Chuck van Zyl’s Star’s End “Gatherings” concert series in Philadelphia, alongside artists including Steve Roach and Robert Rich. “Earthshine” extends his ongoing run of releases on Projekt Records into a new recording method rooted in his earliest analog tape work.
items._cn_summary: 挪威音乐人 Erik Wøllo 的新专辑《Earthshine》由 Projekt Records 发行，以限量300张CD和数字形式推出。专辑共20首短曲彼此无缝衔接，也可作为一整段连续作品聆听。整体以电子音景构建，融合处理过的持续音和序列器脉冲，在情感充沛的段落与稀疏静谧的片段之间交替。创作过程中，Wøllo 重返1980年代的工作方式，使用模拟四轨与八轨磁带机录制，再转入计算机进行编排与混音，试图以更缓慢、更即时的方式捕捉创作直觉，结果产出更为流动开放的音乐。专辑标题借喻地球反射光照亮月球暗面的微弱光辉，呼应其朦胧幽远的氛围质感。文章末尾提供了艺人简介与各发行渠道信息，但内容整体偏向新闻通稿性质，缺乏深入的乐评分析与主观聆听感受。

items.body: 2026.09.16 海外クラシックNEWS～from ドイツ① 海外のクラシック界のニュースやコンサート、オペラ公演の様子を、現地在住の筆者がいちはやくお届け。今回は、ドイツの8月の音楽シーンから、意欲的なプログラムが展開されたベルリン・ムジークフェストのもようをレポートします。 中村真人 Masato Nakamura 音楽ジャーナリスト、フリーライター 1975年、神奈川県横須賀市生まれ。早稲田大学第一文学部卒業後、2000年よりベルリン在住。著書に『明子のピアノ』（岩波ブックレット）、監修を務めた『おとうさんのポス... 詳しく見る 音楽の友 編集部 月刊誌 1941年12月創刊。音楽之友社の看板雑誌「音楽の友」を毎月刊行しています。“音楽の深層を知り、音楽家の本音を聞く”がモットー。今月号のコンテンツはこちらバックナンバ... 詳しく見る 音楽シーズンと共に幕を開ける音楽祭、ベルリン・ムジークフェストが今年も始まった。前身のベルリン芸術週間を含めると今回が75回目という節目で、とりわけ意欲的なプログラムが組まれている。8月28日のオープニング公演が、ニコラス・コロン指揮フィンランド放送交響楽団による、リゲティのオペラ《ル・グラン・マカーブル》であることも、その表れといえるだろう。 20世紀後半を代表するオペラだが、ベルリンでは比較的上演の機会に恵まれている。2003年のコーミッシェ・オーパー（バリー・コスキー演出）、2017年のサイモン・ラトル指揮ベルリン・フィルハーモニー管弦楽団（ピーター・セラーズ演出）に続き、筆者にとっては3度目の実演となる。 「架空の国ブリューゲルランドの国歌が演奏されますのでご起立ください」とアナウンスされ、実際に聴衆が立ち上がってから鳴り響くのが、12個のクラクションによるけたたましい前奏曲。演奏会形式の上演かと思いきや、歌手は全員インパクトの強い衣裳を身につけ、舞台上演に比べて遜色がない。 客席に配したバンダや合唱、子役を使った秘密政治警察「ゲポポ」の登場など、フィルハーモニーの空間を存分に生かした舞台である。ヴィーナスと「ゲポポ」長官の二役を超絶技巧で歌うソプラノのサラ・アリスティドウを始め、歌手陣は総じてすばらしい。フィンランド放送響も、その精緻で美しい響きを生かした申し分のない演奏を聴かせてくれた。 一方、全体主義政治を生き抜いたリゲティが書いた、非人間性や腐敗をテーマにしたこのオペラが、かつてのような風刺性を持ちにくくなっている実情も感じた。現実の独裁政治や自然災害のほうが、はるかにグロテスクかつ巨大な範囲で私たちを襲い続けているということなのだろう。 ではこうした野心的なプロダクションが意味を失っているのかと言えば、そんなことは決してないはずだ。ロシアと国境を接したフィンランドとの共同制作により、このオペラがフィンランドで初演された数日後にベルリンで上演されたことには意義があった。こうした国際的な連携自体が、時に有効な政治批評性を持つこともありうる。 サバール指揮コンセール・デ・ナシオンのメンデルスゾーン～刺激的かつフレッシュな《イタリア》 サバール指揮のコンサートは、もはや一回一回に聴き逃せない重みがある © Fabian Schellhorn ムジークフェスト2日目（8月29日）には、ジョルディ・サバールが手兵のコンセール・デ・ナシオンと客演した。本コーナーで同じ顔ぶれによる今年3月のオール・モーツァルトのコンサートを紹介しているが、サバール指揮の公演はもはや一回一回が聴き逃せない重みを増している。今回のオール・メンデルスゾーンのプログラムも、フィルハーモニーはほぼ満席だった。 メンデルスゾーン「交響曲第3番《スコットランド》」と「第4番《イタリア》」、その間に「序曲《フィンガルの洞窟》」を挟む、一見何の変哲もないプログラムだが、泰斗サバールの手にかかると夢のような時間に変わる。 とくに面白かったのが《イタリア》で、一般的に知られる1833年版ではなく、作曲家がその後手を加えた1834年版がベルリン公演で用いられた。この版で聴くと、とくに第2楽章から第4楽章までの印象がガラリと変わるのだ。 バスのオスティナートで進行する第2楽章は深い祈りのようで、サバールが語るように「J.S.バッハのコラールのような」瞬間さえある（彼はこの楽章をアンコールでもう一度指揮した）。第4楽章のサルタレッロでは、1833年版にはないティンパニの強打が加わり、嵐のように始まる。中間部で弦楽器セクションが目まぐるしいテンポで奏でる音型のやり取りは、ピリオド楽器のコンセール・デ・ナシオンによっていっそう明晰に浮かび上がる。これほど刺激的かつフレッシュな《イタリア》体験は初めてだった。 前半の《スコットランド》では陰影の深さと共に、スコットランドの民族舞踊の生き生きとした表現が光った。ムジークフェストへのインタヴューで、サバールは「私はかつて17世紀の原典を用いて、スコットランド音楽の研究に4年間を費やした」と明かしているが、あらゆる時代と地域の音楽を吸収してきたサバール指揮の演奏には、人間の文化のなかで育まれてきた音楽の「養分」がぎっしり詰まっている。
items._cn_summary: 本文报道了第75届柏林音乐节的两场开幕演出。首先聚焦尼古拉斯·科隆指挥芬兰广播交响乐团上演的利盖蒂歌剧《勒·格兰·马卡布尔》，这部20世纪后半叶的重要作品以讽刺独裁政治为主题，舞台运用了大量空间化元素，包括散布于观众席的邦达管、合唱与儿童演员，萨拉·阿莉斯蒂杜的精湛花腔技巧尤为突出。其次报道了乔尔迪·萨瓦尔指挥的和谐之花古乐团演绎的菲尔斯版《意大利交响曲》与《苏格兰交响曲》，呈现了历史原真乐器演绎与学术研究的深度结合。《意大利》选用1834年修订版，其中第二乐章的贝斯持续音深具巴赫圣咏气质，第四乐章萨尔塔列洛加入定音鼓强奏，呈现出前所未有的刺激与新鲜感。整体报道侧重古典演出实况描述，涉及当代作品与历史演绎的并置。

items.excerpt: 〈環境破壊と資本主義の終焉〉をテーマに深い海の底――意識の深層へと手を伸ばした5年ぶりの新作。ARAKI Shin、marucoporoporo、Kumi Takaharaをゲストに迎え、当人のフィンガー・ピッキングによるギターに微かなノイズや柔和な管絃楽器の音色を重ねた本作がもたらすのは、有機的なアンビエンスと安らぎにも似た静寂。瞑想的な美しさを纏ったポスト・クラシカル作品だ。

items._cn_summary: 中岛元浩时隔五年推出的这张专辑以环境破坏与资本主义终结为主题，将意识比作深海，吉他指弹作为主要载体，叠加微噪声与柔和的管弦乐器音色，营造出有机化的氛围声响与冥想般的静谧美感。专辑邀请ARAKI Shin、marucoporoporo、Kumi Takahara等客座乐手参与，丰富了层次与质感。作为日本独立音乐人作品，该专辑在概念性与氛围营造上具有独到之处，但在声音实验性与跨类型融合深度上仍偏保守，更接近氛围化的当代器乐创作而非前卫实验。整体适合追求内省聆听体验的听众。

items.body: King Ayisoba Pure Confusion King Ayisoba's seventh album was cut live in a single sitting. Everything else was built around it afterwards Pure Confusion by King Ayisoba The most useful thing to know about Pure Confusion is how it was made. King Ayisoba flew to England in November 2024, sat down in Adrian Sherwood’s studio in Ramsgate, and played the whole record in one afternoon. He says the songs were already finished in his head. Nothing about his performance was altered after the fact. The bass, the cello, the saxophone, the harmonica, the dub processing on the desk: all of it was added later, to a recording of a man who was alone in a room with a two-string lute made from a calabash... The post King Ayisoba – Pure Confusion appeared first on The Quietus.
items._genre: world music / experimental / folk fusion / afro-futurism
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑采用了一种极为罕见的录制方式：King Ayisoba独自飞往英国，在Adrian Sherwood的录音室中用一个下午的时间一次性演奏完成整张唱片，所有歌曲事先已在脑海中构思完毕，演奏本身未经任何后期修改。之后贝斯、大提琴、萨克斯、口琴以及dub处理才围绕这段独奏逐步叠加。他使用的乐器是一把由葫芦制成的两弦鲁特琴，散发着浓郁的西非传统声响。Sherwood的制作为这些原始演奏增添了dub质感与器乐层次，使得传统非洲乐器与英国地下制作美学形成对话。作为King Ayisoba的第七张专辑，它体现了一种跨大陆的合作模式——非洲传统乐器与英国实验录音棚的结合。原文为新闻式介绍，乐评深度有限，但制作背景本身具有相当的独特性与文化融合价值。

items.body: “En La Mar”, one of the best loved songs in the Ladino repertoire and one that also travels under the name “La Sirena”, strands a maiden alone in a tower above the sea, calling to the sailors going past, wanting love and wanting out. Rachel Valfer sings her in the Judeo-Spanish that Sephardic Jews took with them when Spain expelled them in 1492 and the Ottoman Empire gave them shelter. David Mac Lean‘s flamenco guitar brings Andalusia back to the song, and the players around it mark where the song went instead: Dan Cantrell on accordion, Faisal Zedan on Arabic percussion, Eliyahu Sills on upright bass and on the bansuri he has played with the group since their first album in 2009. The track comes from Entre Las Huertas, released on 28 August, the third album by the Bay Area’s Qadim Ensemble and the first given over entirely to Ladino. Most of it comes from the kantigas, the songs Sephardic women kept and handed on, so the record runs through lullabies, a wedding party number and a mother unloading about her straying husband while she rocks the baby to sleep. Valfer and Sills have run the group from Berkeley for close to twenty years, she singing in seven languages after six years studying maqam and Persian dastgah in Israel and Palestine, he moving between ney, oud and bass. For this album they went into the studio and played, cutting most of the record live before guests came in with flamenco guitar and qanun. Stream “En La Mar” HERE and take home Entre Las Huertas through THIS LINK The post Daily Discovery: The Qadim Ensemble x Rachel Valfer x Eliyahu Sills – En La Mar appeared first on Rhythm Passport.
items._genre: world fusion / Sephardic / Ladino / flamenco / Middle Eastern
items._cn_summary: Qadim Ensemble 来自加州湾区，由 Rachel Valfer 和 Eliyahu Sills 主持，乐队近二十年专注于跨界融合。专辑《Entre Las Huertas》是他们第三张作品，也是首张完全围绕拉迪诺语（Ladino）展开的唱片。曲目大多源自塞法迪犹太女性世代相传的坎蒂加（kantigas），涵盖摇篮曲、婚礼歌谣及生活歌谣。编曲以弗拉门戈吉他呼应安达卢西亚根源，同时引入手风琴、阿拉伯打击乐、低音提琴与印度 bansuri 笛，标示出 1492 年犹太人流亡后在奥斯曼帝国土地上的文化迁徙轨迹。Valfer 曾在以色列与巴勒斯坦学习马卡姆与波斯达斯加体系，能以七种语言演唱。整张专辑以现场演奏方式录制，再叠加客座乐手的弗拉门戈与卡龙琴层次，呈现出地中海东岸多元文化交织的声响景观。

items.album: Dark Pop Artist Midniter Puts Longing Into Motion in Video for “I Could Love You”
items.excerpt: Don’t you know I could love you better Be your release when you’re under pressure All that you hold, we could hold together I could be, I would be if you let me Somewhere inside I Could Love You is a person pacing around a room, rehearsing the case for why somebody ought to love them back. items.body: Don’t you know I could love you better Be your release when you’re under pressure All that you hold, we could hold together I could be, I would be if you let me Somewhere inside I Could Love You is a person pacing around a room, rehearsing the case for why somebody ought to love them back. Every argument has already been prepared: I understand you, I can carry some of this weight, I can protect you, I can give you something better. None of it changes the verdict. With this new single, Midniter takes us somewhere between genuine tenderness and the dangerous confidence of believing you know what another person needs. Nic Pugh sings it without burying himself beneath theatrical anguish. The melody keeps drawing him toward the same impossible proposition, while piano and synthesizers give the track a strange openness, almost too much room for these thoughts to wander around unchecked. You can hear why Pugh calls it a ballad, although its emotional center feels closer to fixation slowly becoming aware of itself. “I Could Love You came from an old piano tune that I never finished,” Pugh reflects. “The bookends of the song are directly from that idea, with the middle evolving into a more synthpop direction for Midniter. To me, it’s a pretty standard ballad about unrequited love – a tale as old as time that everyone can understand.” The interesting part is how quickly “I could love you” changes meaning when repeated often enough. At first it sounds generous. Later it begins carrying frustration, entitlement, bargaining, hope, and the awful knowledge that intimacy cannot be argued into existence. Pugh keeps returning to the same emotional doorstep because leaving would require admitting that closeness has limits, and that another person can feel affection without crossing the line you desperately want erased. The video carries on this uncertainty, and wisely leaves plenty unexplained. Dustie Bayer moves through quiet Charlotte locations while dancers Audrey Baran, Faith Centa, and Donovan Granville turn physical proximity into something unstable. Bodies meet, separate, lean toward one another, then occupy their own space again. Pugh appears with Joe Boyland and Dan Hitzelberger behind a backlit white bedsheet, reduced to silhouettes, as though desire itself has flattened everyone involved into shapes onto which meaning can be projected. “The video is more ambiguous, playing with the question, ‘Is this about desire, obsession, or both?’ It’s ultimately your call to make. Our goal with this video was to focus more on mood than narrative. It was more important to live in these feelings of distance and longing than explain why they linger. The dancers, our friends from Baran Dance, were instrumental in carrying those moods throughout the video with their choreography. Our main actress Dustie Bayer was also incredible in her debut.” Watch below: Loving somebody from afar can feel noble when told from inside your own head. Midniter lets enough doubt creep into the room to make that certainty increasingly difficult to trust. I Could Love You is out now, coinciding with the launch of vinyl LP pre-orders for Xeno through SugarTank! Records’ new website. Xeno will be released on 27 October 2026. Listen to I Could Love You below and order the track here. I Could Love You by Midniter Follow Midniter: Instagram YouTube Spotify Website The post Desire or Obsession? — Dark Pop Artist Midniter Puts Longing Into Motion in Video for “I Could Love You” appeared first on Post-Punk.com.
items._cn_summary: Midniter的单曲《I Could Love You》从一首未完成的老钢琴曲展开，两端保留原曲的骨架，中段演变为合成器流行的方向。Pugh的演唱不依赖戏剧化的痛苦嘶吼，钢琴与合成器为情绪留出大量空旷空间，使歌曲听起来像在反复推敲同一个不可能的命题——为何对方不应爱自己。这首所谓的情歌在不同重复中悄然变质，从慷慨滑向执念，从渴望变为讨价还价。MV在夏洛特本地取景，舞者以身体接触与分离交替的编排外化了这种不稳定的亲密关系，Pugh与同伴以逆光剪影出现，欲望本身被压缩为可被投射的形状。整首作品聚焦于单方面的注视如何在自洽的叙述里缓慢滑入偏执。

items.body: Spanish producer Nightcrawler releases the single “Reactor 4” on September 17, 2026, the first track from his forthcoming album “Uranium 235” on Nightcrawler Music. An official video accompanies the release. “Reactor 4” mixes dark techno, industrial electronics and cinematic textures. The single and its video take their titles from nuclear engineering, and Nightcrawler describes the video as the first look into the album’s dystopian universe, setting up “Uranium 235” as a concept record built around that imagery. The track was produced, mixed and mastered at NC Sound Studio, Nightcrawler’s own studio. Nightcrawler also directed the video, and cover design comes from George Gold Design, which also created the artwork for the 2025 Nightcrawler and Spammerheads collaboration “Ghostless”. “Reactor 4” arrives on all digital platforms and Bandcamp from September 17. About Nightcrawler Nightcrawler is a Spanish electronic music project active since 2011, built around horror and sci-fi film scores and a mix of dark atmospheres with driving electronic rhythms. The project released the “Strange Shadows” EP in 2014 and built out an extensive Bandcamp catalogue since, including releases such as “Visionary”, “Metropolis” and the “Corrupted System” and “R.U.S.H.” singles. In April 2025, Nightcrawler teamed up with the Valencia-based EBM duo Spammerheads for the collaborative single “Ghostless”, which Side-Line covered at the time. On November 13, 2025, Nightcrawler released the album “Malevolent Forces” through Nightcrawler Music, an eight-track record built on film-inspired EBM and spoken-word samples that Side-Line reviewed. “Reactor 4”, out September 17, 2026, is the first single from the project’s next album, “Uranium 235”. Nightcrawler continues to release music independently through Nightcrawler Music.
items._cn_summary: 西班牙电子音乐人Nightcrawler发布单曲《Reactor 4》，作为即将发行的概念专辑《Uranium 235》的先行曲目。该作品融合暗色techno、工业电子声响与电影化质感纹理，取材自核工程领域的术语，配套官方音乐视频构建出专辑的反乌托邦世界观。整张专辑被定位为围绕核意象展开的概念唱片，所有制作、混音及母带处理均在艺术家自有的NC Sound Studio完成，视频亦由其本人执导，封面设计来自曾合作过的George Gold Design。Nightcrawler自2011年起活跃于电子音乐领域，风格根基源自恐怖与科幻电影配乐，长期在Bandcamp平台保持独立发行节奏，此前作品包括《Strange Shadows》EP、《Malevolent Forces》专辑及与Spammerheads合作的单曲《Ghostless》等。

items.body: Sebastian R. Komor has launched a new project, SRK Group, with the single “Spitfire”, released September 11, 2026 on Infacted Recordings. The Polish-born, Norwegian-raised, Canada-based producer is best known as a longtime member of Icon of Coil. “Spitfire” combines dark electro, EBM and club-oriented electronics. Komor wrote, mixed and produced the track himself at his Xenomorph Productions studio; mastering is also credited to Xenomorph Productions. Describing the song, Komor calls it “personal, loud and danceable.” Spitfire by SRK Group “Spitfire” is available now on Bandcamp and streaming services. About Sebastian Komor Sebastian R. Komor was born in Zabrze, Poland, on May 7, 1976, and moved to Norway in 1981, where he grew up in Fredrikstad’s EBM and industrial scene alongside acts such as Apoptygma Berzerk. He released his first demo in 1992 and recorded under names including Melt, Area51, Sector9 and Moonitor before teaming up with fellow Fredrikstad musician Andy LaPlegua. That collaboration led to the formation of Icon of Coil in 1997; Komor became a full member during the production of the debut single “Shallow Nation” in 2000 and went on to co-write the albums “Serenity Is the Devil” (2000), “The Soul Is in the Software” (2002) and “Machines Are Us” (2004). Komor relocated to Edmonton, Alberta, Canada, in 2004. The following year he started Zombie Girl with Renee Cooper, releasing an EP in 2006 and the album “Back From the Dead” on Alfa Matrix and Metropolis Records in 2007. He later signed to FiXT for the solo hard techno and industrial project Squarehead, released the techno/tribal album “To the Past From the Future in the Present” as Moonitor, and continued his dark techno and EBM alias Komor Kommando, whose releases include the “One By One” EP on Alfa Matrix in 2022. Beyond his own projects, Komor built an extensive catalogue as a producer, mixer and mastering engineer, working with artists including Apoptygma Berzerk, Front Line Assembly, Ayria, Covenant, Circle of Dust and The True Union. His project Bruderschaft brought him together with Ronan Harris of VNV Nation, Joakim Montelius of Covenant, and Stephan Groth of Apoptygma Berzerk. SRK Group, launched with “Spitfire” on Infacted Recordings, is his newest outlet after roughly three decades in the electronic underground.

items.body: Buenos Aires netlabel Cyclical Dreams releases the various-artists compilation “Gemstones VII” on 11 September 2026, the seventh volume of a Berlin School and ambient series the label has issued every September for at least the past three years. The 14-track collection sets contributors from the label’s own artist roster alongside outside acts, working in synthesizer-built ambient, space music and sequenced Berlin School electronics. The ‘Gemstones VII’ tracklist mixes label regulars with outside contributors The album opens with Antike Elektronische Musik’s “Quantum Atlas – Origin” and Alexander Obukhov, recording as Obukhovaudio, on “Plasmadrom”, followed by Wolfgang Merx’s “In Blue” and X-Orbital’s “Timeless Dust Becoming Light”. Aura Merlin contributes “Echo Location”, and Carolyn Fok, whose album “Chrysalis” appeared on Memoir of Sound in 2025, submits “A Leap of Heart (Origin Mix)”. AeTopus adds “Others”, and Cartas de Japón, the band shared by Cyclical Dreams’ three founders, contributes “Faune III”. The second half runs spaceseer’s “Cliffdwellers”, Sophos’s “From Another Time”, and Rodrigo Passannanti‘s “Submerged Industry”, before Kirk Monteux Mysoftmusic’s “Flute Ocean Peace”, the Klaus Wolfe & Castle Waters collaboration “Spirit Bridge”, and Adeptus Mechanicus’s closing “A New Mysterious Beginning”. Cyclical Dreams describes the release as “a walk through beautiful pieces of electronic music inspired by the Berlin School and Ambient music”. Gemstones VII by Various Cyclical Dreams also posted a full-album stream of “Gemstones VII” on its own YouTube channel. “Gemstones VII” follows “Gemstones VI”, released 19 September 2025, and “Gemstones V”, released 13 September 2024, each edition landing in the same week of September for three years running. Side-Line has previously covered Cyclical Dreams releases from D*Time, whose album “Nightwoven” came out on the label in May 2026, and from Christian Wittman, whose album “Andromeda” appeared on Cyclical Dreams in January 2026. About Cyclical Dreams Cyclical Dreams is a netlabel founded in Buenos Aires, Argentina, in early 2020 by musicians Pablo Bilbao, Lucas Tripaldi and Esteban Menash, set up as an outlet for Berlin School, ambient, soundscape, space music and drone electronic music. The three founders play together as Cartas de Japón and also release solo material, including Bilbao’s Pabellón Sintético project and Menash’s M3NASH. Beyond its own roster of artists, Cyclical Dreams runs a Bandcamp store and digital distributor, a mastering service, and the online Cyclical Magazine. The label’s artist roster includes Sophos, the recording name of Argentine composer Ulises Labaronnie, who has worked in music composition and production for 28 years, including the project triØN, film and theatre scores, and music for Cartoon Network video games, alongside concerts in Argentina, Chile and France. Cyclical Dreams has built its “Gemstones” compilation series around annual, dated volumes carrying its own CYD catalog numbers, with “Gemstones V” and “Gemstones VI” preceding this year’s “Gemstones VII” in successive Septembers. The new compilation continues that yearly pattern while again combining the label’s core contributors with outside artists.
items._genre: Berlin School / ambient / space music / electronic
items._cn_summary: Cyclical Dreams 厂牌连续第三年发行的年度合辑《Gemstones VII》收录14位艺术家的作品，聚焦柏林学派电子、氛围与太空音乐风格。曲目阵容既有厂牌旗下固定艺人，也邀请外部音乐人参与，涵盖合成器氛围、序列化的柏林学派电子等手法。三位创始人组成的乐队 Cartas de Japón 贡献了《Faune III》，其他作品来自 Antike Elektronische Musik、Alexander Obukhov、Wolfgang Merx、AeTopus、Sophos 等不同背景的电子音乐人。整张合辑定位为穿越电子音乐片段的漫步，风格统一且叙事连贯。该厂牌来自阿根廷布宜诺斯艾利斯，是独立 netlabel 运营模式，附带母带服务和线上杂志。作为信息性较强的新闻稿式介绍，文章提供了厂牌背景与曲目列表，但缺乏对具体作品的声音分析和深度评论。

items.body: Laibach release “MUSICK : ENCORE” on Mute on 20 November 2026, on vinyl, CD and digitally. The companion piece to this year’s “MUSICK” combines unreleased material from the original album sessions with new remixes from SILVERWINGKILLER, Richard X, The Lincolnshire Poacher and PUNCHBAG. MUSICK : ENCORE by Laibach The album leads with two new tracks. “This Is The End” features Slovenian singer Kaja Skrbinšek, while a new version of “Love Machine,” featuring Balkan vocalist Senidah, is remixed by Mute labelmates PUNCHBAG. Senidah also appears on a second version of “Love Machine,” remixed by UK producer The Lincolnshire Poacher. Electropop producer Richard X co-produced several album tracks and remixes “Resistencia,” which also features MRFY member Gregor Strasbergar. Ghanaian artist Wiyaala, whom Laibach first saw performing in an underground club in Ljubljana, appears on two new versions of “Musick”: the Unsick version and a remix by the band’s own guitarist, Vitja Balžalorsky, credited here as Balžalorsky. Long-time Laibach vocalist Marina Mårtensson features on new track “#US,” which SILVERWINGKILLER also remixes, and on “Faith No More” alongside Joker Out guitarist Bojan Cvjetićanin. Koala Voice frontwoman Manca Trampuš features on new track “Modern Talking.” The vinyl edition carries a 10-track selection; the CD and digital editions expand to 13 tracks with the additional remixes. The digital and CD tracklist: “This Is The End” (feat. Kaja Skrbinšek), “Yom Kippur,” “#US” (feat. Marina Mårtensson), “Tales From The Crypt,” “Faith No More” (feat. Marina Mårtensson and Bojan Cvjetićanin), “Musick” (feat. Wiyaala) (Unsick version), “Resistencia” (feat. Gregor Strasbergar) (Richard X remix), “Love Machine” (feat. Senidah) (PUNCHBAG remix), “#US” (feat. Marina Mårtensson) (SILVERWINGKILLER remix), “Modern Talking” (feat. Manca Trampuš), “Allgorhythm” (feat. Wiyaala) (Algorithm remix, assisted by iTurk), “Love Machine” (feat. Senidah) (The Lincolnshire Poacher remix) and “Musick” (feat. Wiyaala) (Balžalorsky remix). “Yom Kippur” previously appeared as a standalone single featuring the Palestinian Children’s Choir, released in October 2025. On the new material, Laibach state: “Perhaps these are the final moments when creating music purely for enjoyment still carries broader significance – before alien, generative intelligence outplays and outperforms us all. So, we seized the moment.” Laibach tour dates for 2026 Laibach continue the “MUSICK” tour through the autumn with UK and European dates, including a show at London’s Islington Assembly Hall on 29 September: 25 September – Ljubljana (SI), Kino Šiška 26 September – Ljubljana (SI), Kino Šiška 29 September – London (UK), Islington Assembly Hall 30 September – Manchester (UK), Ritz 1 October – Southampton (UK), 1865 2 October – Canterbury (UK), The Gulbenkian 4 October – Gent (BE), Democrazy 6 October – Bochum (DE), Zeche 7 October – Nijmegen (NL), Doornroosje 8 October – Hamburg (DE), Große Freiheit 36 9 October – Oslo (NO), Rockefeller Music Hall 11 October – Copenhagen (DK), Bremen Teater 13 October – Berlin (DE), Huxleys Neue Welt 14 October – Dresden (DE), Reithalle 15 October – Brno (CZ), Fleda 16 October – Zagreb (HR), Boogaloo Further European dates are scheduled into 2027, including Milan, Bologna, Lausanne, Paris, Nancy, Winterthur, Vienna, Budapest, Bucharest, Thessaloniki, Athens and Benidorm. About Laibach Laibach formed in 1980 in the mining town of Trbovlje, Slovenia, evolving out of Dejan Knez’s earlier band Salto Mortale. The group co-founded the Neue Slowenische Kunst art collective with the IRWIN and Scipion Nasice Sisters Theatre groups in 1984. Their name was officially banned in Yugoslavia in 1983 after a controversial television appearance, a ban lifted in 1985 following the release of their second album, “Nova Akropola,” on Cherry Red Records. Laibach signed to Mute Records for their 1987 album “Opus Dei,” which paired subversive cover versions of Opus’s “Live Is Life” and Queen’s “One Vision” with original material, and went on to release “Let It Be” (1988), “Kapital” (1992) and “NATO” (1994), the latter reworking “The Final Countdown” and other pop and military anthems. The band’s best-known lineup – Milan Fras on vocals, Dejan Knez, Ervin Markošek and Ivan “Jani” Novak – carried Laibach through the 1990s and 2000s, spanning albums including “Jesus Christ Superstars” (1996), “WAT” (2003) and “Volk” (2006). Knez left the group in 2003. More recent studio work includes “Spectre” (2014), “Also Sprach Zarathustra” (2017), “The Sound of Music” (2018), “Wir sind das Volk (ein Musical aus Deutschland)” (2022) and the symphonic work “Alamut” (2022), alongside “Sketches from the Red District” and the “Love Is Still Alive” EP, both from 2023. Milan Fras remains lead vocalist, joined by Ivan “Jani” Novak, longtime vocalist and guitarist Marina Mårtensson and guitarist Vitja Balžalorsky. Recent singles have included covers of “Strange Fruit,” “White Christmas” and Bijelo Dugme’s “Top,” released as “Die Kanone” with Goran Bregović in 2025, plus the “Yom Kippur” single that October. Laibach unveiled “Musick” ahead of its 2026 release on Mute, the group’s most pop-leaning album to date. “MUSICK : ENCORE” extends that record with new songs and remixes, arriving 20 November 2026.

items.body: Soft Vein All We’ve Known of Heaven Artoffact Records If you’ve been following Los Angeles’ Soft Vein since their first LP in 2023 but hadn’t heard any of the pre-release singles for new album All We’ve Known of Heaven you might be forgiven for wondering if it’s even the same project. It’s not that Justin Chamberlain has entirely changed his approach to music: you’re still getting a lot of the same melancholic melodies of the project’s debut and sophomore records, but with the hyper-gloomy and often dour mood of those albums replaced with a powerful, hopeful yearning. Coupled with Chamberlain’s rapid growth as a songwriter, All We’ve Known of Heaven has emerged as one of year’s most moving and engaging listens. Chamberlain’s biggest asset in both his songcraft and his performances is his sense of restraint. The album’s feeling of intimacy comes directly from how simultaneously laidback and vulnerable it comes across; a cut like “Forgetting You” works because its clean, Knopfler-esque guitar and multi-tracked vocals bring you in, setting you up for the big drum machine claps and a damnably catchy chorus. The effect is that it feels like the songs being sung to you as a listener, not at you. When Chamberlain asks “Is this all we are?/All we know?” on the jaw-dropping synthpop gem “All We’ve Known of Heaven” it’s a question directed at the world at large, its ruminations on the sad state of things in the early days of the 21st century building to a plea for a kinder, more loving world. It’s stirring by virtue of the honesty with which it’s delivered, both vocally and musically, from its tasteful synthwork and the smooth closing saxophone solo, to the cathartic introspection of its lyrics and Chamberlain’s deeply heartfelt vocals. The warmth and passion of the songs are fully supported by the wonderfully lush and refined production from Chamberlain himself, assisted by live member Andrea Mantione of Nuovo Testamento. “Learning to Talk” is a sweet love song about the sense of discovery in being with another person, its little synth and guitar trills and half-whispered opening verse building momentum gradually, the space around the instruments growing into a powerful climax. In one of the record’s best moments on “Chekhov”, the edge of bitterness and disappointment in Chamberlain’s voice is perfectly matched by the ghostly pads that hang behind him like a reminder, suggesting a soft but everpresent ache. Similarly, the Cocteau Twins guitars that adorn “White Towers (White Shores)” work so well because the song’s programmed drums and keys are locked in beneath them, lifting the song up while also pushing it forwards. All We’ve Known of Heaven is comforting, quietly confident, unhurried, and above all an incredibly lovely record to just sit and listen to. Justin Chamberlain’s willingness to let the songs speak for themselves is certainly a part of it; while no doubt there’s passion and investment in every moment of the LP, it’s all presented with an unpretentious and open candor that makes it easy to get swept up in its grand swells of emotion. An absolute stunner of a album, and one of the year’s best to date. Recommended. Buy it. All We've Known of Heaven by Soft Vein The post Soft Vein, “All We’ve Known of Heaven” appeared first on I Die: You Die.
items._cn_summary: Soft Vein 的第三张专辑延续了洛杉矶冷潮与合成器流行的基底，但在气质上发生了显著转变：前作中浓重的忧郁与阴郁被一种充满希望的渴望所取代。主创 Justin Chamberlain 以高度克制的笔法处理旋律与人声，制造出亲密而脆弱的听觉氛围。专辑制作由 Chamberlain 本人主导，Nuovo Testament 的 Andrea Mantione 协助完成，音色温润饱满。器乐层面展现出不俗品味：Knopfler 式的干净吉他与多轨人声交织，Cocteau Twins 风格的吉他飘浮于编程鼓点与合成器之上，萨克斯独奏为标题曲增添柔光。歌词从个人情感延伸至对当代世界的反思，以诚实的方式探讨失落、爱情与对更美好世界的渴求。整体而言，这是一张舒展、从容、情感真挚的合成器流行之作。

items.excerpt: ナポレオンの出生地としても有名な、地中海に浮かぶフランス領コルシカ島。本作はそのコルシカの伝統的なポリフォニー・コーラスを基盤としながら、地中海に息づく様々な音楽文化を取り込み独自の音楽を作り上げてきたグループ、ラルバの30年以上のキャリアで初となるライヴ盤。三声が神秘的な響きをもって重なり合うア・カペラ・ポリフォニーで始まり、澄んだ歌声によるリード主体の楽曲も織り混ぜながら、ギターやヴァイオリンによる伴奏が海風を運び、中東やフラメンコにも通じる哀愁に満ちた旋律が深い余韻を残す。コルシカの音楽を知らない耳にも新鮮でありながら、どこか故郷を思わせるような普遍的な美しさが胸を打つ異国情緒豊かな作品。

items.body: Corre [koh-ra] Correlate (verb) To have a mutual relationship or connection, in which one thing affects or depends on another… Music collective Corre fuse the natural with the synthetic and the classical with the electronic. The two styles are on opposite ends of the musical rainbow, but they can and do work effectively together, coalescing into one, their unity producing another prime example of music’s deep contrasts and contradictions. The collaboration is only seven months old (beginning in March of this year), and this gives the music a fresh appearance, shooting out electrifying lightning bolts that give the music a healthy pulse of spontaneity as well as a flexibility to rival that of a rhythmic gymnast. Soon to be released on Akira Records, Form is Corre’s debut album. The two collaborators are aiming to create a multi-media, cross-genre alliance, and the first fruits are already ripening – their recent video, created by artist Hattie Ellis, fuses naturalistic photography with a series of digital manipulations – ghosts in the system – to create a thoroughly modern and visually striking film. Opposites supposedly attract, and this blending really works. The modern and the contemporary intermingle with the accepted classical sound – the past shaping the present – sharing the space. One never outstrips the other. In music, all is one… An ambient blurring occurs when the harmonies bathe in a washed-out, slow-burning progression which, in centuries past, could have graced the sheet music in a classical recital. The textures here are a lot thicker. In ‘Response’, a piano repeats a series of soft, gorgeous chords, lights are lowered and the electronics are toned down. Muted electronics with soft edges glide around, and gentle rhythms cycle throughout the tracks. Sometimes, the electronic rhythms are absent, drifting out and away from the track, and that leaves the piano to play on in its layered atmosphere. The notes are as soft as the sea air and are always in transit, but they move slowly and thoughtfully as they go from one place to another. Stuttering, staccato-based rhythms punctuate the muted piano chords with the dash-dot-dash of morse code. Their quick-fire response is a crucial part of the music, capturing the magical thrill of spontaneity and bottling it up. Sometimes, the best things are done on impulse. www.cargocollective.com/correcreative
items._cn_summary: Corre是一支成立仅七个月的二人音乐组合，将自然音色与合成器声响、古典钢琴语汇与电子节奏编织在一起，形成新旧交融的听觉空间。专辑中钢琴以轻柔绵延的和弦铺陈底层氛围，电子节奏有时退场让位给纯粹的键盘独白，有时以断续的摩尔斯电码式短促脉冲切入，捕捉即兴的火花。整体偏向慢速燃烧的渐弱式氛围音乐，音色层次较为丰富，融合策略清晰但实验性有限。乐评来自独立平台Fluid Radio，文字长度充足，属于原创乐评。Akira Records为小众独立厂牌，符合地下发行的定位。该作品对关注氛围与电子跨界融合的听众有一定吸引力，但在声音设计的突破性上仍偏向常规路径。

Though this recording documents the work of thirteen of Belgium's most innovative ensembles, the real star is the Park Abbey located just outside Leuven and founded in 1129. Built and maintained for the purpose of quiet meditation, the abbey hosted the musicians who used the quiet surroundings to prepare and record their unique musical imaginings. The result is a mostly instrumental collection that mines the riches of Belgian folk and world music traditions, including Romani scales,
La Pump
rhythms, and accordion-based
bal-musette
flavors.
For example, Slovenian-native R�n�lius Bikar�s searing violin opens the set with �R�fuge.� He and his self-named ensemble channel pan-European Roma history.
Meanwhile, �Poor Boy� is a Django Reinhardt-inspired swing tune by Charlotte Pelgen & Bipolar Bows. Pelgen sings in English, and with her ukulele strumming sounding very much like a tenor banjo, the tune is enlivened by Lotte Remmen�s St�phane Grappelli-like fiddle lines.
The distinctive sound of the oud announces yet another musical tradition. Blending Mediterranean with Arabic sounds, the Lebanese-Belgian singer Amber Haddad and her trio, oudist Adil Benhsain and double bassist Martijn Vanbuel, spin a beguiling musical web. According to the liner notes (translated from the Dutch), �Tawazden� is about �seeking balance and finding peace within a complex environment.� Further, �the various spaces of the abbey and their murals are the direct source of inspiration.�
The accordion is especially prominent. So too is the Western classical tradition. Sounding almost Baroque, �Sacristia Invisibilis,� is another standout for me. Here, mandolinist Andries Boone is joined by Anouk Sanczuk on octave violin (sometimes called the baritone violin, tuned an octave lower than standard) and on harpsichord Sandra Van der Gucht. They create an indescribable sound you have to hear.
Throughout, the Abbey�s stone presence looms. Aur�lie Charneux�s solo clarinet piece �L'Ape Millenaria� is about a thousand-year-old bee that haunts the abbey. �Thila,� by Enara Navaira, evokes ancient Celts with a jazzy double bass and drum kit behind throat singing and Citera (a kind of Hungarian zither).
Airboxes is a duo who mix chromatic and diatonic accordions. Their offering �Abdij 1� sounds improvised. Again from the liner notes, �they share their impressions of the timelessness of monastic life.�
Despite the wide range of styles,
The Sound of the Abbey
has a coherence, perhaps informed by the artists� shared inspiration. The record is often surprising and always soothing. Three years in the making, the ensembles were lovingly recorded and mixed by Bert Huysentruyt and mastered by Pieter De Wagter from Equus Mastering. They have rendered a warm sound using the natural reverb of ancient stone provided by the project�s silent partner.

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Find the artist online. Further reading: Otava Yo - Do You Love (Review) Sofia Rei - Umbral (Review)

items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. Various Artists - L�ve L�ve (Volume1) (Review) Pedro Lima - Maguidala (Review) Ann O'aro - Bleu (Review)
items.label: Bongo Joe
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了圣多美和普林西比七十至八十年代的Puxa音乐，这是葡萄牙语非洲殖民地中鲜被记录的岛国声音。乐评指出，这些曲目是多元节奏的融合体，混入merengue、soukouss、benga、加勒比元素等成分，构成召唤与驱邪仪式感的舞曲。Pedro Lima领衔的乐队以切分吉他与鼓组交锋，Sangazuza展示了贝斯和键盘抽离后鼓与吉他驱动的疯狂律动。多把吉他交织缠绕、主唱与和声此起彼伏地融入旋律框架，长时间的现场即兴延伸是这类音乐的常态。乐评强调该国地理小却音乐场景丰富，但因缺乏大城市级别的录音基础设施，许多作品未能留存，使该合辑的文化档案价值尤为突出。

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?
items.label: Go' Danish Folk Music
items._cn_summary: 这是一张来自丹麦三人组的数字EP处女作，由北欧民谣场景中经验丰富的歌手Mia Guldhammer领衔。五首曲目以传统音乐为主，融合了铙钹、口琴、风笛、长笛和弦乐等乐器，营造出一种古老而略带粗糙质感的氛围。开场曲以粗犷的节奏展示了Guldhammer极具说服力的嗓音；唯一原创曲目由乐队成员Morten Musicus贡献，呈现出口琴与风笛的推动力；铙钹为传统曲目提供细腻的底色；终曲作为器乐曲融合了口琴、长笛与弦乐，产生出令人兴奋的失衡感。整体呈现出超越新人水准的成熟度，五首曲目已展现出乐队的潜力。

items.body: Kr�ta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Ed�n has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sj�fl�yte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with �Fossgrimen,� a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish �Polska from Per Myhr,� having played a repeated introductory riff on the sj�fl�yte, with Mats Ed�n providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Ed�n who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. It's a short track and almost as soon as it gets going things start to fragment and everything grind to a halt.
items.label: Taragot
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由一位瑞典小提琴家与两位挪威乐手合作，以传统斯堪的纳维亚舞曲旋律为素材，却刻意跳出舞场伴奏的功能定位，转向室内乐式的亲密对话。乐评指出，作品呈现出对音乐深层含义的探索意图，三位乐手模糊了不同音乐类型之间的界限，例如竖笛手采用萨克斯和风笛等挪威传统之外的乐器，打击乐手也致力于跨越流派。选曲上以挪威赛特斯达尔山谷的"瀑布精灵"传说相关曲目开场，暗示民间舞曲表层欢乐之下潜藏的黑暗暗流。演奏中旋律线在乐器之间交接、对位并最终瓦解碎片化，呈现出远离常规民俗演绎的实验性处理方式。
