items.album: Recent Reviews from Touching Extremes
items.excerpt: Touching Extremes recently published the following reviews of experimental music. Eamon Sprod – Foil Void Join Avoid (Aposiopèse) assembles four years of recordings from overlooked interiors and urban infrastructure into two acousmatic suites. Robert Piotrowicz – Wrong Filament (Merkurial) uses synthesizers, asymmetric meters, microtonal inflections, and imagined Eastern European dance traditions across six electronic compositions.
items.body: Touching Extremes recently published the following reviews of experimental music. Eamon Sprod – Foil Void Join Avoid (Aposiopèse) assembles four years of recordings from overlooked interiors and urban infrastructure into two acousmatic suites. items._cn_summary: 本文为Touching Extremes近期发表的实验音乐评论合集，介绍了两张专辑。Eamon Sprod的《Foil Void Join Avoid》耗时四年录制，素材取自被忽视的室内空间与城市基础设施，经整合后形成两套声学作品（acousmatic suites），呈现特定场所的声音特质。Robert Piotrowicz的《Wrong Filament》以合成器为核心，融合非对称节拍、微音程变化以及对东欧舞蹈传统的想象性重构，完成六首电子乐曲。两位音乐人各自从声音源与节奏结构角度切入实验领域，但本文仅为新闻性质的专辑简介合集，缺乏深入的乐评分析，因此可获取的评论信息较为有限。

items.body: The album was originally released during the formative years of Kompakt's long-running Pop Ambient series Photo by David Westlake Markus Guentner's ambient and dub techno classic LP In Moll is being reissued to mark its 25th anniversary. The record has been newly remastered by composer and mastering engineer Rafael Anton Irisarri for its new edition. Speaking about the record, Irisarri said: "It immediately opened a door to a world of music I didn't know existed. Markus showed me entirely new possibilities for what electronic music could communicate." The updated release takes in fresh visual elements created by Guentner himself as he revisited the album 25 years on, while the track 'In Moll 4' will appear on vinyl for the first time as part of... The post Markus Guentner’s ‘In Moll’ Set for 25th Anniversary Reissue appeared first on The Quietus.
items._cn_summary: 本文报道了Markus Guentner经典专辑《In Moll》迎来25周年再版的消息。原文内容为纯新闻稿性质，缺少对音乐本身的深度评论。据介绍，专辑发行于Kompakt厂牌Pop Ambient系列初创阶段，将环境音与dub techno元素结合，由作曲家兼母带工程师Rafael Anton Irisarri重新处理。Irisarri表示该作品曾为他打开电子音乐表达的全新可能。再版加入了Guentner本人重新创作的视觉元素，其中曲目'In Moll 4'首次以黑胶形式发行。作为Kompakt厂牌Pop Ambient系列的重要历史作品，该专辑在德国电子音乐版图中具有标志意义，但原文信息量有限，难以充分评判其艺术价值。

items.album: Some Sort of Better Future: Globo Interviewed

items.body: Jeremy Allen speaks to the recently reinvigorated experimental synth pop band about covering an entire album by The Fall and the changing scene for electronic music Globo have never really fitted in. That was certainly true when the renegade cell of electronically-minded musicians released their debut album Pro War in 1995, armed with just Akai samplers, drum machines and their wits. Comparisons with groups like Underworld were never quite right, and they couldn’t have been any more antithetical to the hedonistic London-centric Britpop parade that so obsessed the inkies at the time.  Formed in Norwich in 1993 by then Melody Maker journalist Mark Wernham (who wrote as Mark Roland), plus illustrator Steve Appleton, filmmaker Paul Thompson and former member Ian McGregor, Globo... The post Some Sort of Better Future: Globo Interviewed appeared first on The Quietus.
items._cn_summary: 这是一篇关于英国实验合成器流行乐队Globo的人物访谈文章。乐队于1993年在诺里奇成立，1995年发行首张专辑《Pro War》，仅凭Akai采样器、鼓机和成员的智慧闯荡乐坛。他们从未真正融入任何音乐流派，既不同于Underworld式的电子舞曲路线，也与当时伦敦中心主义的英伦摇滚风潮背道而驰。文章提及乐队近期重新活跃，并计划翻唱The Fall的整张专辑。文章讨论了电子音乐场景的变化，以及这群离经叛道的电子音乐人在独立场景中的定位。内容偏向访谈报道而非深度乐评，对音乐本身的创作手法和作品细节描述有限。

items._cn_summary: 意大利老牌新前卫摇滚乐队 D'Arcansiel 在沉寂多年后推出新专辑《Hard Times》，以一首近18分钟的史诗开篇曲《Too Late！》展开宏大叙事，主题聚焦地球生态危机与人类行动的迟缓。新任键盘手 Davide Sorella 主导创作，编曲以键盘为核心——合成器、钢琴、大键琴与 Hammond 风琴交织出浓烈的巴洛克新古典色彩，旋律性强且结构庞大。乐评指出其融入了日系 RPI（Rock Progressivo Italiano）传统与 Gryphon 式的复古管风琴元素，整体风格介于深沉哀歌与悲剧性交响之间。虽然评论称其余三首同样出色，但主体仍属于正统交响前卫摇滚范畴，缺乏实验性与即兴自由度，与该用户偏好的实验、前卫、爵士与电子方向契合度有限，但意大利地域特色与 RPI 传统为其增添一定分量。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是前Pain of Salvation贝斯手Kristoffer Gildenløw的第五张个人作品，最初计划于2020年发行，因疫情延后至2024年。前作《Let Me Be A Ghost》以个人抑郁体验为主题，而《Empty》将视角扩展至更宏观的层面，反思人类整体的精神空虚与自我毁灭倾向。音乐延续了他一贯的风格，在梦幻与现实之间寻找平衡，光影交织，营造出悬置般的氛围。歌词探讨迷失、痛苦与对人类无意识的焦虑，由他低沉而具辨识度的嗓音演绎，配器兼具柔情与重量。作为Crossover Prog领域作品，它偏向情感叙事与旋律性表达，在前卫摇滚框架内进行情绪探索，但在声音实验或跨界融合层面着墨有限。

items.body: Review by VianaProghead — Review N� 987"The Roaring Waves" is a collaborative album by two influential names in the European prog scene, Steve Hackett and Steve Rothery. As we know, Hackett was the main guitarist of Genesis and Rothery is the guitarist of Marillion. As we also know, Marillion was the band most close to Genesis of all British prog bands that appeared in the 80's. So, we can say that Rothery is, somehow, the heir of Hackett on guitars. So, we can not be surprised by this collaborative effort.Although the initial idea emerged around 2015, "The Roaring Waves" took nearly a decade to be written and recorded. The sessions were split between the Racket Club (Marillion's studio) and the home studios of both musicians. The strong connection between both solidified on stage when Rothery joined Hackett at the Royal Albert Hall in 2024 to play "Fly On A Windshield", one of the most famous tracks of the album "The Lamb Lies Down On Broadway" by Genesis.So, "The Roaring Waves" is the first instrumental collaborative project between two of the most iconic guitarists in progressive rock. The album is a profoundly cinematic, atmospheric and a melodic work, entirely inspired by the power, mysteries and nuances of the sea, beautifully paced conversation between two master guitarists. Instead of a flashy "speed trial" or shred-fest competition, the album prioritizes compositional patience, atmospheric depth, and melodic trade-offs. Hackett's angular, classical-tinged and experimental approach, merges seamlessly with Rothery's emotional soaring sustain. Having decided to completely forgo vocals and lyrics, the album gives the listener a true complete imaginative freedom through textures that blend progressive rock, classical music, ambient and electronic textures.The line up on "The Roaring Waves" is Steve Hackett (guitar and harmonica) and Steve Rothery (guitar, bass guitar and keyboards). "The Roaring Waves" also had the participation of Riccardo Romano (keyboards and bass guitar), Daniele Pomo and Leon Parr (drums)."The Storm" is the dramatic opening of the album. It begins by placing the listener in the midst of a storm, with the guitars intertwining to create the tension and force of a storm at sea. This is a beautiful, wild and cinematic piece that delights the listener, a track that serves more as an introduction to the album than in a particularly loud announcement. "Sandsend" is a more restful and contemplative track, where the tension eases, evoking a sense of isolation, a cool beauty and serene atmospheres. It veers a measured rhythm, toward elegant and melancholic atmospheres reminiscent of Pink Floyd, letting the guitars literally sing in unison. At under five minutes, the track is correspondingly compact. "Red Dragon" is the shortest track on the album where Hackett introduces the sitar guitar to give the composition a mystical and an oriental sound. It brings a touch of world music to the otherwise rather watertight soundscape with folkloric influences, bagpipes and sitar sounds. This is a more playful and less polished piece than its predecessors. The title track "The Roaring Waves" is probably the most compelling moment on the album. It begins with a beautiful flourish of classical guitar by Hackett. It's one of the album's highlights, the real swell. Slowly, the swelling dynamics, guitars giving each other space, and precisely that blend of melancholy and pathos for both Steves, a real classic prog moment. "K-129" is one of the most experimental and intriguing tracks on the album. Electronic soundscapes and dark guitars create a very own feeling. Once again, this rhythmic framework is layered over the two guitarists in a largely improvisational style. It stands out paying homage to the "Kosmische Musik" and the Berlin School of the 70's. It reminds me of "Gento", by Bisocope of last year, the project of Rothery and Thorsten Quaeschning of Tangerine Dream. For me, it's one of the strongest tracks on the album. "The Black Sea", described by the authors as a dark adventure, was chosen as the lead single of the album. It's one of the album's great melancholic beauties. Rothery's warm guitar meets Hackett's finely crafted timbres. This is precisely where it becomes clear why this collaboration makes any sense at all. "Pacific Coast Highway" departs from the gray and icy atmosphere of the previous tracks, an unexpected track. Here, the music gains rhythm and movement with Hackett playing harmonica and slide guitar, evoking a high-speed car trip along the sunny California coast. It's a lighthearted, road-movie-esque jam with plenty of vocals at the end of it.Conclusion: "The Roaring Waves" is a dialogue between two musicians who respect and listen to each other, and who have acquired the wisdom of guitarists who have nothing left to prove. It's, therefore, a mature, profound and extremely refined work. "The Roaring Waves" remains above all an album on which two guitarists thankfully dedicate themselves not to themselves, but to the respective piece and its shared concept. Hackett and Rothery harmonize superbly with each other, instead of getting lost in an endless competition for the more spectacular solo. Compared with the album "GTR" of Hackettt and Howe, this is a much better work. I know, those were the 80's. But I don't know if it's an excuse.Prog is my Ferrari. Jem Godfrey (Frost*)
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是前Genesis吉他手Steve Hackett与Marillion吉他手Steve Rothery的首张纯器乐合作作品，主题围绕海洋展开。两位吉他手以对话式的方式交替演绎，避免炫技竞争，着重于氛围深度与旋律的克制铺陈。Hackett偏古典化、棱角分明的实验性手法与Rothery情感饱满的延音形成融合，结合了前卫摇滚、古典、氛围与电子质感。全器乐的编排给予听众充分的想象空间。录音跨越近十年，制作分散于Racket Club与两位音乐人的家庭工作室完成。专辑在保持传统前卫摇滚骨架的同时，融入了世界音乐元素如西塔吉他，并以电影化的叙事结构串联各曲目。

items.body: Review by Neuroprog — Octobre is one of the first progressive rock albums from Quebec, released in 1973. The wonderful compositions on this album allow Pierre Flynn to showcase his full talent. He is truly one of Quebec's finest singers, a real hidden gem. Overall, the songs are built around powerful and catchy riffs. This is therefore not the most progressive album out there: it does not particularly seek to push musical boundaries or necessarily build toward epic moments. It is instead one of the great Quebec rock albums, with clear influences from the progressive rock movement of the time. It was only after this album that the band would go on to develop and complicate its compositions further. It is unfortunate that this excellent album and band are not nearly as well known as Harmonium, Robert Charlebois, Beau Dommage, Offenbach, Paul Pich�, and others.More specifically, the album features a lot of changes in rhythm despite containing only eight tracks and running for less than 30 minutes. We go from songs like Si on partait, a more straightforward rock song with a frantic pace, to much more nuanced and slower pieces featuring melancholic lyrics sung beautifully by Pierre Flynn. Flynn also shines on several tracks with his expressive organ and piano solos.To fully appreciate this album, it is essential to understand French, and especially "joual", as well as the Quebec specific references of the period. Dans ma ville is a perfect example of a song built around two completely different tempos. You can feel the musical crescendo throughout the verses before everything comes back down for a gentle chorus, conveying the feelings of anger and nostalgia that run through the song. This combination of emotion and rhythm is present throughout the album, reinforcing the power of Flynn's vocals.The closing track, La maudite machine, is an anthem in which the importance of the lyrics takes precedence over the melody. Strangely enough, it is the best-known song on the album, although it is not necessarily the most musically interesting one.4/5
items._cn_summary: 1973年来自魁北克的早期前卫摇滚专辑，由Pierre Flynn主导，词曲创作围绕强劲抓耳的吉他riff展开，并非以突破音乐边界或构建史诗段落为目标，而是扎根于魁北克摇滚传统，融入当时前卫摇滚运动的元素。专辑仅含八首曲目、总长不到三十分钟，却在节奏变化上颇为丰富，从狂热直接的摇滚曲风过渡到缓慢内敛、带有忧郁法语歌词的段落。Flynn的演唱极具表现力，风琴与钢琴独奏亦是亮点，多首歌曲通过不同节拍段落之间的张力传递愤怒与怀旧等情绪。歌词层面大量使用魁北克特有的方言与文化指涉，若不熟悉法语及当地语境会削弱聆听体验。作为魁北克早期前卫摇滚的代表之一，这张专辑兼具旋律性与情绪深度，但整体取向偏向摇滚框架内的成熟表达，前卫性有限。

items.body: Review by higgins — There are debuts that sound like debuts, with that mixture of timidity and overreach so typical of someone still searching for their place, and there are debuts that arrive already carrying the astonishing confidence of people who've been playing together for half a lifetime without anyone quite noticing. Datura Lodge decidedly belongs to this second lineage. And it's no coincidence: Nicky B and W. have known each other and played together since their teens, something that comes through in every breath of this self-titled album, a chemistry that can't be improvised or bought in any studio, however good it may be.I listened to this record thanks to a promo copy the label was kind enough to send me, and I'm deeply grateful for it, because Datura Lodge is one of those works you'd rather have stumbled upon yourself, tripping over it in a record shop, and yet here we are, with the good fortune of having had it in hand ahead of time.The New Jersey duo doesn't hide its sources, nor should it. There's a melodic streak that leads straight back to Genesis, especially in those moments when the vocal reaches for the hook without giving up harmonic complexity. And there's something else too, something of our own era: that way of organizing the chaos, of metering out the tension and releasing it at exactly the right moment, which inevitably brings to mind a more restrained Steven Wilson, or his band Porcupine Tree on the days it decides to smile.Tracks like "Stone" or "Can" show that technique serves emotion rather than the other way around, with an instrumental display (Adam Holzman is in there on keys, contributing a great deal) that never tips into gratuitous showmanship. But it's in the fragility of "Hole" or the almost uncomfortable honesty of "Them" where Datura Lodge reveals its true nature: an album that knows how to laugh at itself while talking about rootlessness, generational disillusionment, and the strange task of staying human amid a full digital shipwreck.Datura Lodge doesn't reinvent progressive rock, but it inhabits it with a naturalness and a joy of playing that are sorely missed in so many current releases, more concerned with orthodoxy than with life.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张来自新泽西二人组的首张同名专辑，乐评描述其展现出多年默契演奏所积累的成熟与自信。专辑继承了Genesis式旋律性，同时融入Porcupine Tree和Steven Wilson所代表的当代前卫摇滚的节制与张弛管理。键盘手Adam Holzman参与录制，技术服务于情感表达。曲目如"Stone"和"Can"展现器乐实力，而"Hole"和"Them"则呈现脆弱与坦诚，探讨漂泊感、代际幻灭以及数字时代中保持人性的艰难。乐评认为专辑并未重新发明前卫摇滚，却以自然真诚的演奏乐趣栖居于这一传统之中，与许多拘泥正统而缺乏生气的当代发行形成对比。整体偏向传统重前卫范畴，在用户关注的实验、前卫领域中属较为正统的演绎。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — The affirmation often has a psychological value that operates at an unconscious level; it begins from the outside and ends up taking hold internally. The Yes Album was a new beginning for many reasons: the first to feature Steve Howe, the first in which the compositions of Anderson, Chris Squire, and soon Howe would acquire that classic status and the first where rock, jazz, and a distinctive balance between acoustic and electric elements would find their signature style and a home within the progressive universe.There are many classic Yes lineups, and although the subsequent era might be considered the "classic of classics," the 1971 period is already worthy of that title. Gathering at Langley Farm, they recorded a handful of songs that would become enduring favorites, not only for that lineup but for those that followed, and have been performed live ever since.I'm a fan of the Peter Banks era, but Steve Howe, while retaining that affinity for rock 'n' roll, jazz, and classical music, brought a rhythm, a groove, and a fingering style, along with a cosmic dimension, that set the band apart right from "Yours Is No Disgrace." The vocal harmonies, often bordering on a cappella, were just one of many hallmarks that emerged with this album. The band also gained a warmth and an intimacy it hadn't possessed before; tracks like "Yours Is No Disgrace" featured not only instrumental sections but also intimate moments that made for a complete experience."Clap" is the first of many acoustic tracks by Steve Howe; composed of several sections, some with a pastoral, rustic feel and others with a distinct rock-and-roll vibe, the version that made the final cut was recorded live at London's Lyceum Theatre and would forever define one of the facets of this new Yes."Starship Trooper" must be one of the first tracks that made me fall in love with the band. Jon was gradually reaching the peak of his expressive potential, conveying a genuine emotion that was reinforced by Chris Squire on bass, Bill Bruford on drums, and, son, Steve Howe on guitar (who already seemed like a full-fledged member, even though Peter Banks still appeared on the album cover!). There was a palpable sense of communion as they focused on conveying their musical vision. Tony Kaye was solid, too, though he would later be succeeded by someone with such a massive aura that it would elevate "Starship Trooper" to even greater heights. Once again, the vocal harmonies and Jon's voice stood out... and just as the emotion reached its peak, "W�rm", the third section, would kick in. Steve would start off solo, with the rest of the band gradually joining him, creating a soundscape that felt like the prelude to a space voyage and the actual liftoff. And the first of many memorable riffs with an electrifying personality.The emotional momentum didn't let up, as a powerful new surge of feeling arrived with "I've Seen All Good People", a track that is 100% Yes. The band always drew sustenance from both the technical/virtuosic side and the spiritual/emotional one; neither works without the other, and it was their combination that gave birth to their best songs and albums. The track is neatly divided into two parts: the acoustic first section, "Your Move", which carries an almost Andean feel, and the rock-driven second half, "All Good People." The two work in tandem, creating the song's magical contrast."A Venture" is an atypical and unusual track within the context of the �lbum, and a very beautiful one. It features very interesting breaks and syncopated drum and guitar work from Howe and Bruford; towards the end, Chris's bass and Tony Kaye's distinctly jazzy solo leave you wishing they would keep playing like that for even longer."Perpetual Change" is the final track, and Bill Bruford's presence is as notable as it is significant; the format, an elaborate introduction leading into a fully developed song, set a precedent for what was to come. Hints of a country feel followed by a jazz-inflected progression, along with the polyrhythms and counterpoint in the finale, exemplified the band's high level of technical proficiency. Meanwhile, the vocal interplay between Jon and Chris offered a different facet, helping to create an album that holds a unique place in history. There are many layers to consider: while the band's subsequent work was undoubtedly more complex and elaborate, and is rightly regarded as some of their best, this album possesses its own distinct value. It stands as an equally great record, not for the same reasons as the later material, but for others; after all, as we have seen, Yes is a multi-dimensional band.

items._cn_summary: 1971年Yes乐队的第三张录音室专辑，标志着乐队新阶段的起点——Steve Howe作为吉他手首次加入，与Jon Anderson、Chris Squire、Bill Bruford及Tony Kaye共同确立了乐队标志性的声学与电声融合风格。专辑收录了多首后来成为Yes经典曲目的作品，包括开场曲《Yours Is No Disgrace》、Steve Howe的现场录制独奏曲目《Clap》、三段式结构宏大的《Starship Trooper》，以及旋律与和声俱佳的《I've Seen All Good People》。Steve Howe的吉他风格融合了摇滚、爵士与古典音乐元素，为乐队增添了独特的节奏感与宇宙感维度。Jon Anderson的人声与多声部和声是专辑的重要标志，乐队在编曲中展现出器乐段落的复杂展开与亲密段落之间的平衡。整体而言，这张专辑在摇滚、爵士与古典之间找到了独特的融合路径，为后续前卫摇滚的经典时代奠定了基础。

items.body: Catherine Ringer, vocalist, songwriter, and co-founder of French new wave duo Les Rita Mitsouko, has died at age 68. Her children announced her death in a statement to AFP, confirming that she died from cancer on the night of September 14, 2026. With her partner in music and life, Fred Chichin, Ringer made pop music feel large enough to accommodate almost anything: punk impatience, funk, cabaret, electronic experimentation, and the expressive possibilities of French chanson. A song could be funny, sensual, disconcerting, and profoundly sad within the same few minutes. Ringer gave each feeling its own physical presence, singing with a freedom that made conventional ideas of good taste seem rather timid. Born on October 18, 1957, in Suresnes, near Paris, she was the daughter of painter Sam Ringer, a Polish-born Jewish Holocaust survivor, and an architect mother. She left school at 15 and pursued an artistic education through theatre, music, and dance. Among the formative figures in her life was Argentine dancer and choreographer Marcia Moretto, who became her teacher and collaborator. Those years onstage helped establish the connection between movement and voice that would distinguish her work with Les Rita Mitsouko. Nostalgie’s biography documents her early performances and work with Moretto. Ringer met Chichin in 1979, beginning a partnership that would carry them from the Paris underground to international recognition. Their self-titled 1984 debut, recorded with Conny Plank, introduced a group whose appetite for experiment came with a formidable instinct for melody. As Coilhouse’s retrospective observed, Ringer’s background in avant-garde theatre remained visible in the duo’s performances and videos. Marcia Baïla became their breakthrough. Written in remembrance of Moretto following her death from cancer, it joined the exhilaration of dance to the shock of losing someone whose life had been devoted to movement. Its popularity carried that private grief into public celebration. The song offers an especially poignant way to remember Ringer now: affection, anger, and delight sharing the same space, with no easy separation between them. Directed by Philippe Gautier, the music video for Marcia Baïla gave the song an equally extravagant visual life, with costumes by Jean Paul Gaultier and Thierry Mugler. Watch the video below. The duo’s collaboration with Tony Visconti on The No Comprendo in 1986 brought Andy, C’est comme ça, and Les Histoires d’A. The album won at the 1987 Victoires de la Musique, as did Jean-Baptiste Mondino’s video for C’est comme ça. These songs remain an excellent introduction to Ringer’s range: the teasing insistence of Andy, the sharp attack of C’est comme ça, and the ease with which she could make a repeated phrase feel like an argument, an invitation, or a joke. Their creative world extended well beyond records. Jean-Luc Godard included the duo at work in his 1987 film Soigne ta droite, while collaborations brought them together with fellow musical eccentrics. Sparks joined them for Singing in the Shower, from 1988’s Marc & Robert, a meeting of artists who understood how much pleasure could be found in pop’s peculiar corners. Later, Iggy Pop appeared on My Love Is Bad, preserved alongside their other collaborations in the band’s collected catalogue. The apparent playfulness could also carry terrible knowledge. Le Petit Train addressed the deportation trains of the Holocaust, a history bound closely to her father’s survival. Its video, filmed in Bombay, placed Ringer amid exuberant dancing while the words described people being carried toward their deaths. The tension between the music’s invitation and the lyric’s meaning remains deeply unsettling. She understood how a familiar pleasure could open an audience to something painful. Chichin died from cancer in 2007, aged 53, the year Les Rita Mitsouko released Variéty. Ringer continued performing their songs while building a solo catalogue that included Ring n’ Roll in 2011 and Chroniques et fantaisies in 2017. With Plaza Francia, alongside Gotan Project’s Eduardo Makaroff and Christoph H. Müller, she explored tango on 2014’s A New Tango Song Book. Her later work also returned to the intimacy of spoken language. In L’Érotisme de vivre, she performed the poetry of Alice Mendelson, accompanied by pianist Grégoire Hetzel under the direction of Mauro Gioia. The scale had changed, but the curiosity remained: another writer, another setting, another way to give words a body. Ringer leaves music full of appetite and contradiction, open to beauty without becoming polite about it. She made eccentricity feel generous, something an audience could participate in. Our thoughts are with her family, friends, collaborators, and everyone who found freedom in her voice. Follow Catherine Ringer: Instagram Facebook Follow Les Rita Mitsouko Instagram YouTube Bandcamp The post Catherine Ringer, the Extraordinary Voice of Les Rita Mitsouko, Has Passed Away at 68 appeared first on Post-Punk.com.

items.excerpt:

items.body:
From mosh pits to dangdut ring dances, AXEAN Festival 2026 made a case for just how wide — and connected — Southeast Asia’s music landscape can be.

Held at Jimbaran Hub in Bali, the festival’s latest edition welcomed more than 4,000 attendees across its three-day run, including private events. The figure was nearly double the previous edition’s attendance, bringing artists, fans, delegates, and music professionals together for live performances, conversations, and plenty of cross-border discovery.

At the heart of the festival was the music itself. Across three stages supported by TuneCore and EMPIRE, AXEAN offered audiences a chance to move between sounds, scenes, and cultures — sometimes within minutes.

“I love seeing people enjoy music regardless of genre, style, or language,” shared AXEAN Festival co-founder and co-team leader Piyapong Muenprasertdee, also known as Py. “At AXEAN someone might be moshing in a pit one minute and joining a dangdut ring dance the next, which is exactly what happened this year.”

That spirit came into full view during Ndarboy Genk’s set. Bringing together dangdut, koplo, and Javanese pop, the Indonesian headliner turned the crowd into a communal dance floor — the kind of genre-crossing exchange AXEAN was built to encourage.

Bali became part of the festival itself

Returning to Bali for the third consecutive time also allowed AXEAN to deepen its ties with the island’s creative community.

According to Py, the addition of more popular Indonesian acts helped bring in a larger local audience. Beyond Jimbaran Hub, the festival partnered with Craft Hotel in Ubud and Amplitude skate park in Seminyak for pre-event activities, including panel discussions and performances by Balinese artists.

The festival grounds also expanded beyond the traditional showcase format. A Southeast Asian street food hawker centre and an arts and crafts area opened up the experience to younger attendees and families, adding another layer to the community atmosphere.

Connections happened onstage and off

AXEAN’s role as a meeting point for the regional music industry remained just as important as its live programme.

Speed meetings, pitching sessions, and panel discussions connected music professionals from different markets, while partner activities included brunches hosted by Sounds Australia, Korea Spotlight programming by the Korea Creative Content Agency (KOCCA), and initiatives involving France’s Centre national de la musique (CNM).

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by KOCCA MUSIC(코카뮤직) (@koccamusic)

A VIP lounge supported by The Orchard and the festival’s closing after-party gave artists and delegates more informal spaces to meet beyond scheduled sessions.

The result reflected AXEAN’s larger purpose: not simply putting Southeast Asian artists onstage, but creating opportunities for the people behind the region’s music to meet, exchange ideas, and build relationships.

KEXP made its first move into Asia

One of the edition’s biggest developments happened beyond the festival stages.

AXEAN partnered with KEXP for the Seattle-based music platform’s first-ever presence in Asia, becoming its first Asian festival partner for Live at KEXP. 12 Southeast Asian artists filmed and recorded performances at Locca Sea House and Puri Bhagawan, two locations overlooking the sea from Jimbaran’s cliffs.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Diana Ratsamee (@sabaidi.ana)

“KEXP reaches an international audience that Southeast Asian artists rarely get in front of,” Py said. “This time, twelve of them are now in it.”

For a festival built around music discovery and export, the collaboration extended AXEAN’s mission beyond the people physically gathered in Bali and towards a wider international audience.

Building a bigger Southeast Asian music ecosystem

Since launching during the pandemic, AXEAN Festival has developed from virtual editions into an in-person meeting point for the region. Across seven editions, it has featured more than 290 artists from 23 countries, welcomed over 530 delegates from 36 countries and territories, and drawn close to 22,000 live attendees, according to festival figures.

Its latest Bali edition showed what those numbers can look like on the ground: fans moving between genres, artists finding new audiences, and industry professionals meeting counterparts from across Asia and beyond.

AXEAN is already looking towards its next edition, alongside complementary initiatives including a post-festival songwriting camp. Music discovery and export will remain central to that direction.

“Our long-term vision is to raise the Southeast Asian music ecosystem and strengthen its place within the wider Asian one,” Py shared.

If this edition was anything to go by, that ecosystem is increasingly finding a place to meet — and dance — together in Bali.

Like what you read? Show our writer some love!

items.body: Love songs have spent a century turning devotion into a virtue simply because somebody found a chorus for it. Modern Friend’s Pictures takes that old bargain and puts a collar around its neck. Writing from the perspective of a dog, Voytek Korab considers the peculiar compromises of modern relationships, where being wanted can mean learning to live entirely on somebody else’s terms. The affection may be real, but the conditions deserve a closer look: be available, be agreeable, and please do not need anything inconvenient. A founding member of My Favorite Robot, Korab has spent years inside underground electronic music, playing everywhere from Coachella and DC-10 to the Rex Club and Montreal’s Piknic Elektronik. Modern Friend grew from a different urge, one he had been carrying for much of the last decade: get back to singing, get back to writing songs, and give a more personal voice to the ideas taking shape around the music. Pictures, the third single from the forthcoming debut album Nothing Out Of Something, carries that return into a brisk new-wave frame where melody and discomfort share the same room. The beat moves with tidy motorik efficiency as Korab keeps the vocals languid and dreamy. The hooks settle in quickly, making an inviting setting for a less comfortable question about what people are willing to surrender in exchange for being wanted. “I hope to one day be your best accessory” gives the joke its sharpest point. Here, a prospective partner is already negotiating their own reduction, volunteering to fit whatever space another person has available. You can be a modern man’s best friend, provided you remember that “stay” is an instruction and not a promise. “Just put up pictures when I’m lost” brings a more tender possibility into the song through the familiar image of lost-dog flyers fastened to streetposts. Beneath the joke sits a vulnerable hope: if I go missing, care enough to come looking. Korab describes the feeling beneath the song’s humor: “It’s a song about wanting to be loved for who you are, while quietly realizing that sometimes love can begin to feel more like possession, decoration, or convenience than connection.” That distinction gives Pictures its emotional weight. The pet becomes a metaphor for the partner who learns to accept affection on somebody else’s schedule, gradually editing out the needs and opinions that might spoil the arrangement. Small concessions accumulate until one person’s comfort determines the shape of both their lives. Being needed can feel reassuring enough to postpone asking whether that need leaves room for your independence. Korab keeps the premise playful, but the imbalance is familiar: one person waits faithfully for attention while the other decides when to give it. Watch the video for Pictures below: Mixed by Justin Drake at Bakehouse Studios in London and mastered by Ali X in Mexico, Pictures gives its uneasy observations an appealing pop finish. Its easy movement suits the satire: the song makes accommodation sound pleasant enough that you can understand how somebody might overlook the cost. By the end, Pictures has made its canine perspective uncomfortably familiar. Modern romance is for the dogs when loyalty becomes an expectation and affection remains a reward. Even the most faithful companion deserves more than an occasional scrap of attention. Listen to Pictures below and order the single via Permaculture here. items._cn_summary: Modern Friend 的这首单曲以狗的视角切入现代亲密关系中的不对等——被需要与被拥有的微妙边界。歌词在幽默与不安之间游走，以'走失狗海报'的意象承载脆弱的期待。制作上采用新浪潮框架，机械节拍规整推进，旋律简洁上口，却包裹着对'爱的条件性'的审视。Korab 兼具地下电子音乐背景与回归歌曲创作的初衷，使得这首作品在流行质地下保留了一层冷峻的社会观察。总体而言，旋律与主题之间的张力是作品最有趣之处，但声音层面并未提供太多实验性突破。

items.body: Diary of Dreams are releasing a new two-track single, “Der Dunkelheit” / “My Vertigo,” through Adrian Hates’ own label, Accession Records. The German darkwave act is pressing it as a limited digipak CD single and, for the first time on this single, a marbled 7-inch vinyl, each capped at 700 copies; no wider release date has been confirmed yet, and pre-orders have just opened through the label’s trade channels. Accession Records describes the release as “a brief interlude on the way to the album ‘Chapter 2,'” bridging the wait and building tension ahead of the next full-length. “Der Dunkelheit” (“to Darkness”) runs 5:57 and builds a sombre, meditative atmosphere, while “My Vertigo,” at 4:03, leans into the more electronic, catchy side of the project. Both songs will also be played live on the band’s November 2026 tour, which precedes “Chapter 2,” described in the same announcement as the second part of an open-ended concept series, expected in 2027. Diary of Dreams opened that series with the mini-album “Dead End Dreams – Chapter 1,” released on Accession Records on 31 October 2025, and Hates has said of the story it tells that the series ends once the story has been fully told – so “Chapter 2” continuing that arc fits the pattern, though Accession Records has not yet confirmed the album’s exact title. No Bandcamp page, official video or streaming link for “Der Dunkelheit” / “My Vertigo” is public yet, so no embed or pre-order link is included here. Diary of Dreams tour dates in November 2026 Both new songs will be played live when Diary of Dreams tour Germany in November, with support from HINFORT: 19 November 2026 – Schwerin, Germany – Club Zenit 20 November 2026 – Braunschweig, Germany – KufA Haus 21 November 2026 – Bielefeld, Germany – Stereo Live Club 22 November 2026 – Oberhausen, Germany – Kulttempel 26 November 2026 – Wiesbaden, Germany – Schlachthof 27 November 2026 – Jena, Germany – F-Haus 28 November 2026 – Bremen, Germany – Kulturzentrum Lagerhaus About Diary of Dreams Diary of Dreams is the German darkwave project of Adrian Hates, formed in 1989 and built around his voice, programming and guitar. Hates founded Accession Records in 1995, and the label has released the project’s catalogue since, from “End of Flowers” (1996) through “Melancholin” (2023) and the orchestral set “Under a Timeless Spell” (2024). Diary of Dreams performs live with additional musicians including Dejan, Gaun:A, Torben Wendt and Felix Wunderer. In October 2025, the project opened a new open-ended concept series on Accession Records with the mini-album “Dead End Dreams – Chapter 1,” a title drawn from a line in “Panik?” on the 2002 mini-album “PaniK Manifesto.” “Der Dunkelheit” / “My Vertigo” is the project’s next release on the way to “Chapter 2,” the next instalment in that series, and arrives alongside a run of November tour dates across Germany.

items.body: Karine Polwart has proved herself to be an exceptional talent as a singer and songwriter for many years, all the way back to her time with Malinky (the song �Thaney� was a revelation). As a solo artist she�s grown and continually expanded her horizons, coming now to Windblown , a project that began life seven years ago, when Polwart, along with sound designer and composer Pippa Murphy, was artist in residence at Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. The album, with its stage show and book, tells the story of the garden�s oldest specimen, a Sabal palm tree ( Sabal bermudana ), which was gently felled in 2021, and contained a surprise nobody had expected. The tree is the starting point. From there, imagination runs free. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan It�s an album of voice and piano (the outstanding, sympathetic Dave Milligan), and, for all its global outlook on connections, one that�s very rooted in Scotland. You can hear it on the opening track, �Hear The Rigging/Last In Line,� where the melody becomes a slow, aching lament that would sound completely natural on the pipes. The stripped-down sound gives the songs both crafted stateliness and real intimacy. Each one is an exhalation, a memory, a celebration and exploration, with recurring phrases in the words and music acting as touchstones � or even hooks; they certainly stick in the mind. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan In many ways, this is a modest album, with piano, voice and light, judicious soundscaping. It won�t overpower with noise. Yet at the same time, it�s epic, a look at history, at the flow and grandeur of nature, and the things we all carry within us. The music, and especially Polwart�s warm, compassionate voice, envelop the listener, and makes them a participant, not an observer, but a part of the journey and the history. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan The irony arrives at the end, when the venerable old tree is down, and seeds are examined. What people for two hundred years had believed to be a Sabal bermudana turns out to be something different, a Sabal mexicana � and one of the small plants fill grow where it�s forerunner once stood. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan Like music, plants keep to a different time � and this album/book/show give the tree the requiem it deserves, as well as hope for the future. items.body: Sudan Dudan is a Norwegian duo, Marit Karlberg and Anders Erik R�ine, who have released four albums over the last twenty years. On M�rke refrenger , their fifth, they are joined by Hans Hulb�kmo and Magnus Skavhaug Nergaard, contributing instrumentally and with the production. There are eight songs on the album with accompaniment principally led by acoustic guitar, augmented by fiddles, langeleik, lyre, jaws harp and more. The opening track, �Gard og grind� (�Fence and gate�) is a fine introduction to what is to come: finger-picked acoustic guitar, fiddle, bass and snare-drum played with brushes leading into the harmonized vocal, together creating an alluring sound drawing the listener in. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The mood of the album, reflected in its title which translates as �Dark Refrains,� is not always dark, but most of the material, including the title track, certainly has a reflective quality. According to the press release �the lyrics smoulder with unease about the present and the future, while looking back to the myths and riddles of the past. They speak of the earth, the sun, the moon, stars and planets, of lost brothers, quarrelling sisters, loss and grief, of the power of imagination, and of the answers to the simplest and most difficult riddles.� The lyrics of all the songs, in Norwegian, are included in the sleeve notes and while a hasty online translation can aid with some understanding, the full meanings tend to remain cryptic, but there is a sense that words and music complement each other. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan For all its dark moodiness, M�rke refrenger does have its lighter moments. �Bagatelle� recalls and reinvents the melody of a well-known French song, adding some off-kilter harmonies, while �Rulleball� is more characteristically Norwegian, employing a vocal style known as tralling in which words are replaced by a vocalization of the melody, originally used to accompany dances when no instrument was available. No translation necessary there. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The final track �Skriften p� veggen� (�the writing on the wall�) features, for the only time on the album, electric guitar. The sound is deep and twangy, shades of Duane Eddy or a David Lynch soundtrack and it works very well. All in all a fine, imaginatively conceived and beautifully produced record, available as a download or vinyl. Find the artists online. items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

(Review)

Genuine Negro Jig
(Review)

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._genre: field recording / spoken word / sound documentary
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑并非传统意义上的音乐作品，而是声音工程师Ian Brennan在芝加哥南区街道录制的口述历史素材。二十五位遭受枪支暴力影响的居民在九十四岁老人家的前廊上讲述亲身经历，参与者年龄从十七岁到六十七岁不等。录音中保留了大量环境声，没有添加任何配乐，仅有少量即兴说唱。录制当天恰逢特朗普下令国民警卫队进驻芝加哥，地理上靠近奢华的辉煌大道，却是被遗忘的暴力高发社区。文章通过编辑按语而非正式乐评的形式呈现，强调项目收益将捐赠给反暴力公益机构。作为田野录音与社会声音文献具有独特价值，但缺少音乐性元素，与实验音乐或世界音乐的核心定义存在距离。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由意大利热那亚鼓手Andrea Orlando创作，属于意大利前卫摇滚传统。从乐评内容看，文章用大量篇幅梳理了演奏者的履历背景，包括与Finisterre、Höstsonaten等乐队的渊源，以及与低音手Zuffanti为核心的热那亚前卫摇滚圈的联系。专辑邀请了多位圈内乐手参与，如Zuffanti本人担任贝斯，Boris Valle弹钢琴，Luca Scherani和Agostino Marco分别负责键盘和Moog独奏，乐器编制以传统键盘、钢琴、鼓为核心，配器上延续了七十年代PFM以来的意大利前卫摇滚血脉。整体文章更像是一篇详尽的人物谱系考据，对音乐本身的听感和创新着墨较少，以爵士、电子或实验融合视角看缺乏对应的前卫性，属于传统流派内的延续之作。

items.body: Review by ZowieZiggy — Mark one in concert! A a very rare document. I discovered oit recently TKX to YouTube. And since I am a HUGE Purple fan (since December 1970...), I listened to it and decided to post a reviw about this concert. Purple played at Inglewood as guest for Cream!The audio is quiete good I must say. And what we'll get here is a kaleidoscope of all Mark I albums.The good point (at least in IMHHO) is that the band is not going to improvise too much on such numbers as "Mandrake Roots" as well as "Wring that Neck". Two numbers from their own compositions that will be over extended during the Mark II era. Up to almost half an hour!So, here they will be played in a "classic" way, and that's very fine.The covers are very ell rendered and sooooo pleasant as well: "Help!" is gorgeous. And i have to admit that Rod's vocals work perfectly here. His tone of voice is pretty adequate I must say. and I'm gnerally not very laudatory about it to say the least. So, when it is good, one has to ackowledge, right?My fave of all is "River Deep, Mountain High". almost 10 minutes starting with the theme from "2001, A Space Odissey" and there after, rocking quite well.Even if there won't be many readers about this live album, it gives a pretty good feeling about what were the Mark I concert. And therefore my interest.The band sounds very united and happy to play together. But in the background, things might have been different, hence the sacking of Rod & Nick a year later. Leading to the most fabulous (IMHO) period of Purple. Namely Mark II.This live set ends with their biggest hit, nameley "Hey Joe" that will rank in the US Bilboard.All in all, this is a pretty good record. I rate it with 4****.
items._cn_summary: 本乐评聚焦于Deep Purple 1968年加州Inglewood现场录音，这是一张极为罕见的档案级现场专辑，当时乐队作为Cream的暖场嘉宾出演。评论者详细描述了音频质量良好，乐队演奏涵盖了Mark I时期作品，包括长达近半小时的《Mandrake Root》和《Wring that Neck》等原始版本。翻唱曲目如《Help!》和近十分钟的《River Deep, Mountain High》（以《2001太空漫游》主题开场）展现了乐队当时的演奏水准。Rod Evans的嗓音表现获得正面评价，乐队整体状态团结愉悦，尽管一年后成员更替。评论者给予四星评价，认为这张唱片虽读者有限，但忠实呈现了Mark I时期现场演出的风貌。

items.body: Review by arcane-beautiful — The Roaring Waves by Hackett & Rothery sees 2 prog rock guitar legends coming together to create a very enjoyable if slightly tedious instrumental album. No one can take away the impact Steve Hackett & Steve Rothery have on the progressive rock world, with early Genesis & Marillion being a massive influence on the entire modern prog scene since the 70s & 80s, and their monumental playing is always an ace card. But while they bring such talent to these bands, they are the type of guitarists who contribute to a group more than themselves as solo instrumentalists. But the noticeable styles between the 2 are noticeable and they do compliment each other well. The tracks are very well composed and performed, but there isn't too much meat on the bone. It is overall very well mixed too. I'd give this a high 6 to low 7 out of 10. The track I'd recommend is The Roaring Waves.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是两位前卫摇滚吉他传奇人物的合作作品，前者来自早期Genesis，后者来自Marillion，两人的演奏风格在专辑中形成互补。作为纯器乐专辑，曲目编排与混音质量均获肯定，但评论者指出整体内容稍显单薄，缺乏足够的深度，两位乐手虽技艺精湛，却更适合在乐队语境中发挥，而非以独奏器乐人身份撑起整张专辑。推荐曲为同名曲The Roaring Waves。

items.body: Review by Hector Enrique — Although the Trans-Siberian Orchestra project was already well underway following the success of 1996's "Christmas Eve & Other Stories", Jon Oliva and Savatage still had a lot to offer as a band. Thus, in 1997, the American band released their tenth album, "The Wake of Magellan". A conceptual rock opera inspired by the reflections of an elderly and solitary former sailor, H�ctor Del-Fuego Magellan -a fictional character who claims to be a descendant of the famous Portuguese explorer Ferdinand Magellan- whose story is intertwined with various contemporary events (the 1996 murder of Irish journalist Veronica Guerin for her investigations into drug trafficking, and the stowaways on the freighter Maersk Dubai, whose dramatic fate also unfolded that year).The sound of the sea in the instrumental and cinematic "The Ocean" and the festive, Broadway-esque track "Welcome" set the stage for H�ctor to begin a bitter retrospective on his life, ranging from the despondency reflected in dramatic power ballads like "Turns to Me" or "Morning Sun"-crowned by Al Pitrelli's superb and forceful guitar solos- to the seething helplessness and the decision to end his life out at sea, channeled through corrosive, heavy riffs in the '80s-style "Another Way" or the psychotic "Blackjack Guillotine" and "Paragons of Innocence," tracks that draw on influences spanning a wide spectrum from hard rock to metal.The atmosphere of mounting tension that pervades the album reaches its highest peaks in the progressive track "The Wake of Magellan" -an epic that stands as the album's crowning jewel, built upon the wall of sound created by Johnny Lee Middleton on bass, Jeff Plate on drums, and Oliva on piano, culminating in spirited polyphonic harmonies- and in the stormy instrumental "The Storm," featuring another great solo by Pitrelli. And it is only in the theatrical and epic "The Hourglass" that the conflicted character finally finds solace in redemption and a purpose for his life."The Wake of Magellan" is not only an ambitious rock opera but also one of Savatage's most conceptually rich works.Very good.3.5/4 stars
items._genre: progressive metal / rock opera / hard rock
items._cn_summary: Savatage的第十张专辑《The Wake of Magellan》是一部概念摇滚歌剧，以虚构角色——自称葡萄牙航海家麦哲伦后裔的退休老水手Héctor Del-Fuego Magellan的独白回忆为主线，将他的生命反思与1996年爱尔兰记者Veronica Guerin因调查贩毒被谋杀、以及货船Maersk Dubai偷渡客的悲剧命运交织在一起。开场曲《The Ocean》以海浪声效营造电影感氛围，《Welcome》带有百老汇式的欢快气质，随后通过《Turns to Me》《Morning Sun》等戏剧化的抒情曲目展开主人公对人生的绝望回顾，Al Pitrelli的吉他独奏为这些段落增添了力量。专辑的张力在同名曲《The Wake of Magellan》中达到顶点——由贝斯、鼓和钢琴构成的音墙之上发展出复调人声和声，而《The Storm》则是一段充满风暴感的器乐间奏。最终，《The Hourglass》在剧场化的史诗氛围中让角色获得救赎与生命的意义。作为一张结构宏大的概念专辑，它融合了硬摇滚与金属元素，在器乐编排和叙事架构上展现出一定野心，但整体仍处于主流金属摇滚范畴。

items._cn_summary: 1962年8月，巴西制作人Aloysio de Oliveira将波萨诺瓦的奠基三人组Tom Jobim、Vinícius de Moraes与João Gilberto首次聚于录音室，这是巴西音乐史上具有标志意义的时刻。在六周时间内，这批核心创作者完成了这一历史性的合作录音。从文章内容来看，这是一张以原声吉他、轻柔人声与巴西传统节奏为核心的波萨诺瓦经典录音，属于巴西流行爵士传统的源头之作。该专辑对世界音乐历史具有重要文献价值，展示了波萨诺瓦如何将桑巴的韵律与爵士和声相融合，但对于追求前卫实验与即兴语汇的听众而言，其风格偏向温暖抒情的主流爵士路线，实验性与前卫性较为有限。整体而言是一张历史地位高于听觉刺激的经典录音。

items.body: VNV Nation, the British-Irish futurepop and EBM project led by Ronan Harris, released “Automatic” on 16 September 2011 through Anachron Sounds. The album turns 15 this year. Harris recorded it at the band’s own studio between May and August 2011, wrote the words and music, produced it, and made the artwork. It was the eighth VNV Nation studio album, issued in Europe as a CD digipak, with the North American physical CD following on 25 October 2011. In its first week it entered the German Media Control chart at number 8, the duo’s first top ten placing there, and stayed three weeks. It also reached number 66 in Austria, number 77 in Switzerland and number 50 in Sweden, and spent four weeks at number 1 on the Deutsche Alternative Charts. VNV Nation’s ‘Automatic’ tracklist and credits The record runs ten tracks: “On-Air”, “Space & Time”, “Resolution”, “Control”, “Goodbye 20th Century”, “Streamline”, “Gratitude”, “Nova”, “Photon” and “Radio”. “Control” went out as a free download ahead of the album without being issued as a single, and “Nova” picked up German radio airplay. VNV Nation at the time were Harris and Mark Jackson. André Winter handled additional mix production and mixed the album with Harris, and Miles Showell mastered it at Metropolis Mastering in London. Ben Wolf shot the photography. Copies sold on the road during the Automatic tour in 2011 were signed and hand-numbered by the band. The album stayed in the live set long after that. Across December 2016 and late 2017 the duo ran the Automatic Empire tour, playing “Automatic” and “Empires” almost in full, leaving out only “Photon” from the former and “Firstlight” from the latter. A double vinyl edition followed in clear and black pressings, reported here in VNV Nation reissues ‘Automatic’ on double vinyl (clear/transparent + black). About VNV Nation Ronan Harris grew up in Dublin, where radio introduced him to Kraftwerk, DAF and The Human League. He joined a band called Die Fabrik in 1983, moved to London in 1989 and began writing under the name Nation, then relocated to Toronto in 1990. In 1994 he revived the project as VNV Nation, taking the initials from his motto “Victory Not Vengeance”. The first release, “Advance and Follow”, appeared in 1995. Harris has described it as a set of demos rather than a finished album, and a 2001 reissue, “Advance and Follow 2.0”, added re-recorded vocals and five bonus tracks, two of them Front 242 covers. “Praise the Fallen” followed in 1998. Through the same period Harris wrote for Side-Line and served as the magazine’s webmaster until 1999. “Empires”, released in 1999, spent seven weeks at number 1 on the Deutsche Alternative Charts. “Futureperfect” arrived in 2002, built entirely with software synthesizers, and around that point Harris and Apoptygma Berzerk‘s Stephan Groth were credited with coining the term futurepop. Mark Jackson, the band’s live drummer since the mid-1990s, was by then the second half of the studio line-up. “Matter + Form” came in 2005 and topped the DAC albums chart, and “Judgement” followed on 4 April 2007, written and recorded in the band’s own room inside the Soundfactory Studios complex in Hamburg. The box set “Reformation 1” reached Europe on 24 April 2009, which pushed the next album back. Harris told Side-Line the title referred to the 3 things that people desire and which can make you or destroy you, and “Of Faith, Power and Glory” reached Europe on 19 June 2009. “Automatic” followed in 2011 and “Transnational” in 2013. The orchestral collection “Resonance: Music For Orchestra Vol. 1” was recorded at the Babelsberg Studios outside Berlin in February 2015 and released that 15 May, reaching number 7 on the official German album chart. Jackson’s departure in November 2017 was reported in Exclusive : Mark Jackson leaves VNV Nation. Read full statement., with the band’s statement saying he had left to pursue other paths in life. Harris continued alone. “Noire” arrived in 2018, covered in VNV Nation releases new album ‘Noire’ – Out now, on Anachron outside North America and on Metropolis Records in the United States, and it carried the project’s first official music video, reported in VNV Nation debuts official video for ‘When is the future’. “Electric Sun” followed on 28 April 2023, covered in VNV Nation has a new album out, ‘Electric Sun’, 5 years after previous studio album ‘Noire’, and Harris talked through that record in the Side-Line piece VNV Nation interview: ‘Life goes on, the world goes on’. North American dates with Traitrs ran into 2024, announced in VNV Nation launches extra North American tour dates with Traitrs. “Construct” arrived on 9 May 2025. Fifteen years on, “Automatic” sits in the middle of that run as the record that gave VNV Nation their first German top ten album.

items.body: Dillinger Escape Plan co-founder and drummer Chris Pennie’s electronic duo Hipster Slaves releases the new single “Fine Young Hands” on 25 September 2026 through Bald Freak Music. The track pairs electronic rhythms with a synthpop hook built around themes of nostalgia and longing, and arrives with an animated video the duo produced themselves. Hipster Slaves release ‘Fine Young Hands’ on Bald Freak Music Hipster Slaves pairs Pennie, also known for his work with Coheed and Cambria, with singer, synth and piano player Ron Scalzo, the founder of Bald Freak Music. Scalzo sings and plays synths from Nashville while Pennie handles drums, synths and guitars from New York City. “Fine Young Hands” follows the project’s self-titled 2019 debut EP, and Bald Freak Music has a full-length Hipster Slaves album planned for 2027. The single is available to pre-save ahead of release through a DistroKid hyperfollow page, which links to a Spotify pre-save and to the duo’s Bandcamp page. The official video for “Fine Young Hands” is out now on YouTube. About Hipster Slaves Hipster Slaves is the electronic duo of Ron Scalzo and Chris Pennie. Scalzo founded Bald Freak Music, an independent record label and production house, in 2005, releasing his own work in the electronic project Q*Ball alongside guitarist Ron “Bumblefoot” Thal, as well as albums from Bumblefoot, Black Pig and Swashbuckle. In 2006, Scalzo joined guitarist Brett Aveni and Dillinger Escape Plan drummer Chris Pennie to form the alternative rock band Return To Earth, whose debut album, “Captains of Industry,” followed that year. Return To Earth signed to Metal Blade Records and released its second album, “Automata,” in 2010, reunited in 2020, and released “Oblivion” through Bald Freak Music in 2022, followed by the four-song release “Octavius” in 2024. Pennie co-founded the mathcore band The Dillinger Escape Plan with guitarist Ben Weinman in 1997 and remained its drummer through the band’s early catalog before later serving as the drummer for Coheed and Cambria between 2007 and 2011. He also contributed drums to releases by Idiot Pilot, The Armed and Greg Puciato. Hipster Slaves released its self-titled three-track debut EP, featuring the songs “Pitchforks,” “Hipster Slaves” and “Near Dark,” on Bandcamp on 11 November 2019. Scalzo also hosts the Independent Minded podcast and The Joy of Bob Ross podcast, both produced through Bald Freak Music. “Fine Young Hands,” out 25 September 2026, is the first new Hipster Slaves single since that debut and precedes a full-length album the duo has planned for 2027.

items.body: Swedish goth pioneers The Bizarre Orkeztra have reissued “Land” as a 2026 remaster, out now through COMEDIA in collaboration with Ambush Records. The track is the first release in a new series of remastered singles drawn from the band’s catalog. “Land” was written by Sonny Jansson and originally released in 1984 as a 12″ single on Ambush Records, the band’s own indie label. The original tracklist, “Land,” “Korridor,” “Justice” and “Travelling Man,” was recorded by Christer Björklund at The Bizarre Orkeztra’s headquarters, with vocals recorded by Jomma Sundström at Gävle Ljudstudio and production by Bob Boxkopf. Copies of the 12″ came with an eight-page comic booklet, “The No! COMIX No.2,” made specifically for the release. For the 2026 edition, the title track has been remastered by Håkan Nilsson, with Richard Solstjärna serving as executive producer and providing the new cover art. The single is available digitally, including on Spotify, with a release date of 16 September 2026. COMEDIA describes the campaign as presenting “carefully selected highlights drawn from the band’s impressive back catalog.” It is not the first time “Land” has reached digital platforms: the track was previously issued as a remastered digital reissue in 2020, at the time as part of a monthly reissue project with a companion schedule that also covered “Visions On The Wall,” “Midnight Show,” “A Beautiful Place,” “Hunger For Pleasure” and “She’s Got.” The 2026 edition relaunches that catalog campaign as a new series of remastered singles. About The Bizarre Orkeztra The Bizarre Orkeztra formed in Gävle, Sweden, in the early 1980s, emerging from the punk rock band PF Commando and the avant-garde post-punk band Modaern Art. The band was among the first goth acts in Sweden. Its original lineup was Sonny Jansson on vocals and guitars, Richard Sandberg on drums and guitar, and Ola Claesson on bass and backing vocals; Håkan Nilsson later joined on synthesizer for the group’s later recordings. “Land” was the band’s debut release under The Bizarre Orkeztra name, following the 1981 recording “Ingen kärlek, Inget hat,” released under the group’s earlier name, Bizarre Sex. Two studio albums followed on Ambush Records: “Visions On The Wall” in 1985 and “A Beautiful Place” in 1987, along with the singles “Midnight Show” in 1986 and “She’s Got” in 1989. The album “Hunger For Pleasures,” released in 1988, featured Joakim Lindgren on saxophone alongside Nilsson’s synthesizer work. The band released three albums and several singles in total before disbanding in the late 1980s. Bass player Ola “Toli” Claesson, who died in 2009, created cover art for several of the band’s albums and singles, including the comic strip made for “Land,” which was handed out to the audience at the band’s first concert in Gävle. COMEDIA’s new remastered singles series revisits that catalog, beginning again with the track that first introduced The Bizarre Orkeztra to record buyers in 1984.

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — The Bardic Depths are back with Peter Jones contributing as a full member (one of my favorite collaborations that he's done). This is their fourth studio album release of this decade. 1. "Islands" (8:37) excellent and fresh feeling music based on NeoProg sound palette and stylings. I really like the construct, feel, and flow of this song though it does lag a bit in places. (18.333/20)2. "Fallen Leaves" (3:03) GENESISian 12-string-with-organ and anachronistic melody lines open this as harmonized vocal "doo-doo-doo" lines become woven within the instrumental weave. As this pattern continues--throughout the entire song--I find myself rather surprised--and delighted. It's a really cool and fairly inventive (if �tude-like) piece. (8.875/10)3. "Arribabok" (4:48) borrowing a lot from George Harrison/The Beatles' Indian-influenced soundscapes (which were later further developed by the likes of Daevid Allen with his GONG and other projects as well as Steve Hillage and even Peter Gabriel and David Torn). I love Gareth Gole's Torn-Hillage-like guitar tone and play in the third minute. The vocal and congestion and crescendo at the end of the third minute reminds me of both Peter Gabriel's world music and Karl Jenkins' ADIEMUS music. Nice sax play by Peter in the fourth minute and then a nice d�nouement and return to the original palette in the final minute. (9.125/10)4. "October Sun" (8:12) More excellent vocal-centric NeoProg music that reminds me of the fine fare of both FISH ON FRIDAY and TONY PATTERSON (as well as Dave Longdon-era BIG BIG TRAIN). Though the song construct and instrumental play is rather simple and sedate, the bass and vocal work is quite excellent. I understand how solid, comforting "bedding" of easy-to-digest music can serve as an excellent foundation for the exploration/expression of more sincere ideas above it--and this does happen in this song's second half--and I understand the talent and skill it takes to render such a "bedding"--so I am not as critical of this habit or tendency as I used to be (always looking for the sophistication and instrumental virtuosity in each song). I actually really appreciate the way the band has constructed and rendered this song. (17.75/20)5. "From Empty Trees" (4:41) an instrumental opening that sounds like something Tony Banks would have done for Genesis (or himself?) back in the breakout period of the band's popularity. Gareth's guitar work in his lead time during the third minute is okay but nothing very innovative--and the ascending four-chord motif that follows feels so much like Tom Johnson's "Uncertain Smile" ending jam from his 1983 The The album, Soul Mining (with that amazing piano solo from Jools Holland). (8.75/10)6. "A View" (6:18) a gorgeous NeoGenesis weave of arpeggiating keyboard and acoustic and electric guitars with solid low end support from well-coordinated bass and drums also sees some excellent synth strings orchestra and old Mellotron threads in the weave as Peter sings with his usual folk-bard-like approach. Nice weave of multiple other guitar and keyboard lines topped off by a nice heavily-reverbed sax solo from Peter in the fourth minute which is then followed by a fine electric guitar solo. Peter's voice and vocal styling is so classic, so powerful, so iconic. It's no wonder he's been the vocalist of so many 21st Century NeoProg classics. (8.875/10)7. "Harder to See" (4:09) a little more sophistication, syncopation, and frequent key changing makes this an interesting tune--especially when attending to Peter's vocal (he's got to be spot on for this one!) Once the pattern of the four chord motif is established (almost Van Morrison "Moondance"-like), the music becomes more familiar and, thus, comfortable. The chorus and follow-up d�nouement and fade out come easily but are not quite the finish one might hope for. (8.875/10)8. "Rewind" (9:21) this one opens up as another acoustic guitar- and piano-dominated weave that incorporates a four-way vocal approach, lead and harmonies, reminding me of MOON SAFARI as well as bands like Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young or even Wobbler and The Beach Boys. Nice instrumental work in the instrumental section from the third minute to the fifth and then again after 4:40 when things switch to a more ambient/atmospheric palette. (Who's playing the flutes?) This is very psychedelic in its pastoral dream-like feel--very similar to some of Steve Hackett's best stuff ("Cinema Show," Wind and Wuthering, and his early solo albums). Interesting that the the rest of the song (and album) plays out with this atmospheric instrumental weave--five minutes of it (not unlike that odd prolonged ending to "Dancing with the Moonlight Knight")! Luckily, it's really nice! The boys are obviously serious students of the masterpieces of prog's Golden Age. (18.5/20)Total Time 49:09The band's NeoProg music has continued to develop, progressing into more sophisticated and original realms of prog--that remind me of both Peter Gabriel and Fish On Fridays. With any lineup that includes prog-savant Peter Jones one cannot help but have high expectations. The problem comes with the frequent disappointments that come with the feelings of "underdeveloped," "not fully-realized" or "falling short" of possible potentialities. B+/4.5 stars; an excellent album of creative, top-notch NeoProg from some of England's most reverential and proficient veterans. Highly recommended--especially if you like the NeoProg sub-genre where it might be considered an essential masterpiece.
